## Full annotations

<a id="beneath-surface-agent-evolution"></a>

## Beneath the Surface: What We Overlook When We Talk About Agent Evolution

**2026-11-05 · preprint · arXiv preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.07624)

**Mechanism.** Separates repeated success, task coverage, regressions, component interactions and candidate retention in harness evolution. EvoAudit diagnoses archived runs; AGE installs four fixed operator revisions into an A-Evolve recipe while preserving model and evaluator contracts.

**What changes:** Agent code, Prompts / context, Skills, Workflows. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Training/validation task feedback and archived traces drive harness edits; post-hoc diagnostics inform fixed evolution-operator revisions.

**Evaluation.** Compares four adapted evolution recipes across two harnesses and two task domains, with eight-pass evaluations, component interventions and frozen transfer tests.

**Boundary.** Repeated evaluations are not independent evolution runs: AGE uses search seed zero and twenty generations. Operator redesign bundles four changes and uses evidence from the studied settings. Transfer varies by metric and domain; framework-adapted recipes are not unchanged original implementations.

**Code / data.** [Official artifact](https://github.com/simple-agent-lab/RSIHub) — Paper-linked RSIHub framework README inspected. Current framework availability does not establish a pinned reproduction of this paper's artifacts or results; nothing was executed.

**Topics:** architecture, workflows, prompts, skills, recursive-improvement, evaluation. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-11-07.

[Source 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.07624) · [Source 2](https://arxiv.org/html/2611.07624v1) · [Source 3](https://github.com/simple-agent-lab/RSIHub)

<a id="harnessflow"></a>

## HarnessFlow: MCTS-Guided Harness Optimization for LLM Agents

**2026-11-04 · preprint · arXiv preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.06254)

**Mechanism.** Uses a fixed coding agent and tree-based selection policy to search complete executable harnesses. The archive retains successful and unsuccessful refinements; the highest-validation harness is reused with a fixed executor model.

**What changes:** Agent code, Prompts / context, Workflows. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Automatic validation scores, prior code edits and execution traces; a supplied component library supports proposals.

**Evaluation.** Uses fifteen candidate attempts per benchmark across six agent, coding and web benchmarks, disjoint validation/test splits, component controls and an additional executor setting.

**Boundary.** A stronger model proposes edits, and the outer search rules remain fixed. Execution-cost comparisons exclude harness search. The second-executor study reruns optimization rather than transferring a frozen harness; matched candidate counts are not equal end-to-end compute.

**Code / data.** Official implementation availability was not established in this review; no research code was executed.

**Topics:** architecture, workflows, prompts, evaluation. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-11-09.

[Source 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.06254) · [Source 2](https://arxiv.org/html/2611.06254v1)

<a id="targeted-guidance"></a>

## Stabilizing On-Policy Targeted Guidance in Agentic Reinforcement Learning

**2026-11-03 · preprint · arXiv preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.05266)

**Mechanism.** Combines GRPO with on-policy distillation from the same model conditioned on localized feedback. Distillation applies only to failing turns and includes reasoning tokens; learned behavior persists in model weights.

**What changes:** Model weights. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Coding rewards, auxiliary criterion rewards and designed textual hints on failing agent turns.

**Evaluation.** Studies tool-format correction, final-response style and interleaved per-turn requirements in a multi-turn coding harness using an SFT-adapted Qwen3-Coder-30B.

**Boundary.** Hints and reward criteria are supplied. High distillation weights can still collapse performance. Table uncertainty is variability over the last training steps, not independent training runs. Broad held-out agent transfer and autonomous learning of the feedback procedure are not established.

**Code / data.** Official implementation availability was not established; no code or training was executed.

**Topics:** model-training, tools, evaluation. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-11-08.

[Source 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.05266) · [Source 2](https://arxiv.org/html/2611.05266v2)

<a id="route-to-remember"></a>

## Route to Remember: Adaptive Memory Selection for LLM Agents

**2026-11-03 · preprint · Author reports NeurIPS 2026 PALM workshop; primary venue record not verified. · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.05636)

**Mechanism.** Distills session information into a persistent LoRA adapter using student-generated answers scored by a context-conditioned teacher. A verify-then-regenerate reader checks the adapter’s answer against a merged text store and uses the adapter-free model to regenerate unsupported answers.

**What changes:** Model weights, Memory. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Memory-derived synthetic questions and a frozen base-model teacher conditioned on recent memory guide per-user adapter updates.

**Evaluation.** Compares weight and text memory on 1,438 native HaluMem questions, delayed re-asks, and LoCoMo, with training-recipe, routing, and model-scale analyses.

**Boundary.** Recent-fact gains weaken as memories age. Routing improves overall accuracy but lowers the HaluMem conflict-category score. Refusal depends on synthetic unknown-answer training, and the paper identifies judge/rubric errors. Lower read-token use is not a complete cost result: writing is expensive and token accounting omits distillation compute.

**Code / data.** An official implementation was not established in the inspected sources; no code or training was run.

**Topics:** memory, model-training, continual-learning, evaluation. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-11-06.

[Source 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.05636) · [Source 2](https://arxiv.org/html/2611.05636v1)

<a id="rescopebench"></a>

## Towards Robust Long-Lived Agents: Benchmarking Experience Lifecycles in Evolving Environments

**2026-11-03 · preprint · arXiv preprint · core · benchmark**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.05450)

**Mechanism.** Pairs task streams with retained versus cleared memory, skills and retrievable history. Silent environmental changes invalidate selected experience; separate metrics track task outcomes and saved structural/rule knowledge.

**What changes:** Memory, Skills. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Tool observations and permitted later outcome feedback; private reference inventories are used only for scoring.

**Evaluation.** Tests twenty models on 352 tasks across eighteen simulated environments with twenty-six controlled changes, using programmatic task graders and model-judged memory coverage.

**Boundary.** Each model–environment comparison uses one stream per condition, and action-induced environment states may diverge. Coverage is not the precision of all stored content; recovery time measures first completion rather than sustained correctness. Background skill review adds computation outside foreground tool counts, and simulated applications are not live deployments.

**Code / data.** [Official artifact](https://github.com/JoeYing1019/ReScopeBench) — Paper-linked repository and README inspected; no installation, benchmark execution or result reproduction.

**Topics:** memory, skills, continual-learning, evaluation, applications. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-11-08.

<a id="meta-square"></a>

## Meta$^2$: Precomputing Reusable Knowledge for Online Harness Evolution in Long-Horizon Agents

**2026-11-03 · preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.05139)

**Mechanism.** Learns a textual Meta-Skill offline, then freezes it to guide a separate evolver at checkpoints within each task. Bounded notices, instructions, hooks and tools alter the ongoing run without resetting its environment. Harness edits are discarded between runs; the model and offline learning procedure stay fixed.

**What changes:** Skills, Prompts / context, Tools, Workflows. **Persistence:** both. **Learning signal:** Training-only terminal verifier outcomes and privileged verifier-informed rollouts supply act, avoid and hold contrasts. Fixed reflection, aggregation and update prompts turn them into reusable guidance; online decisions use the active trace and permitted workspace evidence.

**Evaluation.** ArXiv v1 tests 60 held-out Terminal-Bench tasks with five repetitions and 75 DeepSWE tasks with three. It reports repetition-level variation, component/reset and checkpoint ablations, and separate construction/deployment costs. A second backbone uses a separately learned Meta-Skill.

**Boundary.** Independent rollout contrasts do not identify an edit’s causal effect; the appendix also discloses worker-prompt and segmentation differences in no-evolver comparisons. Repeated evaluation does not measure variation in rebuilding the Meta-Skill. Costs depend on reuse volume, and code, audit effectiveness and broader transfer remain unverified.

**Code / data.** Author project page inspected on 2026-11-09 and explicitly labels code as coming soon. The full paper includes prompts, algorithms and learned Meta-Skills, but no released implementation or independent execution was established.

**Topics:** prompts, skills, workflows, architecture, recursive-improvement, evaluation. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-11-09.

<a id="continual-autoresearch"></a>

## From AutoResearch to Continual AutoResearch: Do Agents Learn Across Tasks?

**2026-11-03 · preprint · core · benchmark**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.05108)

**Mechanism.** Compares persistent sessions and workspaces with reset instances of the same research agent on matched task streams and time budgets. Separate first-solution, search-efficiency, and final-selection metrics distinguish reuse from better research outcomes. Insight-card interventions isolate explicit memory from session continuity.

**What changes:** Memory. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Visible development data and execution feedback guide research; hidden test scores are computed afterward.

**Evaluation.** Evaluates five native CLI agents across nine ML task families, typically with 30-minute budgets and three-to-five-task streams. Persistence improves aggregate search efficiency, but final-performance gains vary; stricter initialization controls remove the general search advantage.

**Boundary.** Four agents use one matched run pair per stream; one agent has three repeats. Cross-agent differences also include harness differences. The explicit-memory ablation covers one stream, and short related-task sequences do not establish long-term or open-ended scientific improvement.

**Code / data.** The manuscript promises code with its camera-ready version; a runnable release was not established. Nothing was executed.

**Topics:** memory, continual-learning, evaluation, applications. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-11-06.

[Source 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.05108) · [Source 2](https://arxiv.org/html/2611.05108v1)

<a id="benign-skill-misalignment"></a>

## Can Benign Skills Induce Misaligned Behavior in LLM Agents?

**2026-11-03 · preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.04299)

**Mechanism.** Compares fixed-model agents with and without reusable benign skills under matched requests and tools, then studies benign-feedback skill evolution, retrieval relevance, content ablations, and a pre-execution guard. Measures executed safety violations separately from completion of harmful objectives.

**What changes:** Skills. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Successful benign traces and benign validation feedback build and refine skills; harmful-task outcomes are reserved for evaluation.

**Evaluation.** Studies five backbones on AgentHarm, LPS-Bench, and SafeAgentBench. Reports utility gains alongside increased unsafe-action rates, including violations in trajectories that never complete the harmful objective.

**Boundary.** Harmful requests are supplied at evaluation; this is not spontaneous misconduct during benign use. Unresolved trajectories without identified violations are excluded from unsafe-action rates. Some judgments use an LLM; content ablations also change length and wording. The guard terminates blocked runs, reduces benign utility, and leaves residual violations.

**Code / data.** An official runnable artifact was not established in this review; no attacks or research code were executed.

**Topics:** skills, safety, evaluation, applications. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-11-06.

[Source 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.04299) · [Source 2](https://arxiv.org/html/2611.04299v1)

<a id="artifact-to-capability"></a>

## Artifact-to-Capability: Diagnosing Breaks in Capability Formation of Self-Evolving Agents in a Controlled Environment

**2026-11-03 · preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.04952)

**Mechanism.** Tests artifact formation, behavioral change, useful action selection, preservation during composition, and extension across versions. Frozen-system interventions compare identical board states, complete games, and successive code versions rather than treating accumulated artifacts or higher scores as sufficient evidence of learning.

**What changes:** Memory, Skills, Agent code. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Game outcomes and traces drive the evaluated evolvers; independent game rules diagnose retained artifacts.

**Evaluation.** Studies Gomoku adaptations of Reflexion, Voyager, and DGM with one shared backbone, 1,876 fixed states, game traces, and a version lineage. Finds legality-only gains, conflicting skill composition, and later loss of previously passing states.

**Boundary.** These are study-specific adaptations in one rule-enumerable game, not replications of the original systems. Many diagnostic states come from DGM evolution games. Longer evolution, repeated training runs, other backbones, and open-ended transfer remain untested; the five-property definition is a proposed diagnostic framework.

**Code / data.** An official runnable artifact was not established in the inspected sources; no code was executed.

**Topics:** evaluation, memory, skills, recursive-improvement. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-11-05.

## A State Change Is Local, Its Consequences Are Not: Dependency-Aware State Revision for Long-Term Agent Memory

**2026-11-02 · preprint · arXiv preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.02912)

**Mechanism.** Maintains versioned memory states, proposes support dependencies from interaction histories, and checks them with counterfactual model judgments. Revisions propagate selectively, retaining independent support and historical states instead of invalidating every related record.

**What changes:** Memory. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** New evidence, scoped state conflicts and model judgments of dependency strength and alternative support.

**Evaluation.** Reports dependency and cascade-revision tests on 50 constructed StateChangeBench cases with one backbone, plus supplementary memory benchmarks.

**Boundary.** The same model proposes and verifies dependencies. Run counts and the double-annotated subset size were not retained; action-decision and premise-gate results were omitted because their aggregation could not be reconstructed. Small depth strata lack significance tests, and closure consistency is not independent correctness evidence.

## Can Coding Agents Sustain Continual Evolution without Forgetting?

**2026-11-02 · preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.03219)

**Mechanism.** Studies sequential evolution of Mini-SWE-Agent prompts, control flow, and tools with a fixed backbone. Adapted AHE and Meta-Harness optimize one task type and then another; manual trace analysis and edit ablations investigate verification, workflow, and budget conflicts.

**What changes:** Agent code, Prompts / context, Tools. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Task execution traces and benchmark outcomes drive harness edits; prior-task reevaluation measures retention.

**Evaluation.** Examines six source-to-target directions among sampled SWE-bench Verified, paraphrased SWT-Bench, and FeatureBench tasks. Reports severe earlier-task losses and analyzes 520 execution trajectories.

**Boundary.** Uses one backbone and reused subsets of 50, 50, and 30 tasks; no disjoint held-out evaluation is described. Scores are not full-benchmark results. These are study-specific implementations and pairwise transitions, not evidence that every harness or longer task sequence must forget.

## Evolving Memory, Learning to Meta-Control: Test-Time Adaptation for Experience-augmented LLM Agents

**2026-11-01 · preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.01747)

**Mechanism.** Retains episodes and distilled guidance across tasks. A contextual bandit learns whether to solve directly, retrieve cases, retrieve guidance, or distill guidance before solving. Only the small routing models and external memories change; the backbone LLM stays frozen. An optional retry loop also reuses failures within a task.

**What changes:** Memory, Model weights. **Persistence:** both. **Learning signal:** Task outcomes update linear bandit estimates; trajectories and feedback drive language-model memory revisions.

**Evaluation.** Compares four backbones on BigCodeBench, SWE-bench Verified, MultiChallenge, and six BBEH tasks, separating first-attempt success from success within four attempts. Shared-memory and frozen-controller ablations examine routing.

**Boundary.** One run per benchmark/backbone; 100 BigCodeBench tuning tasks remain in its evaluation stream. Outcomes require test or judge feedback, and token accounting excludes evaluator calls. Gains vary by setting; the action space and learning procedure remain fixed.

## Skill++: Towards Lifelong Agents via Routing-Aware Skill Refinement

**2026-10-31 · preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.00544)

**Mechanism.** Rewrites an incoming skill’s name and description to clarify supported capabilities and scope relative to nearby skills. The revised metadata persists in the growing library; earlier metadata, skill bodies, and router weights stay fixed.

**What changes:** Skills, Prompts / context. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Incoming skill bodies, similar earlier skills, and body-derived synthetic queries guide metadata rewriting without evaluation labels.

**Evaluation.** Tests incremental versions of SRA-Bench, SkillRet, and SkillRouter across five routers, plus native Codex CLI skill selection. A separate 150-query, 87-skill check measures hidden-test task success.

**Boundary.** Main outcomes measure required-skill selection, not completed tasks. The principal stream deliberately adds confusable non-substitutes, using model judgments during construction. Random additions show smaller gains. End-task validation uses an early library and an added workflow prompt; it does not establish success at maximum library size.

## Learning to Live: A Step Toward Lifelong Embodied Intelligence

**2026-10-30 · preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.00180)

**Mechanism.** Combines a separately trained streaming perception gate, evidence-preserving robot memory, and ReSight’s Explore–Distill–Mount process. Retained observations can acquire new indexes, and solutions can become reusable tools and skills. Runtime memory/tool updates are distinct from the gate’s offline LoRA training.

**What changes:** Memory, Skills, Tools, Model weights. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Temporal labels train perception adapters; selected observations, task difficulty, and execution feedback support memory and tool construction.

**Evaluation.** Tests perception and selective writing on streaming benchmarks, reuses ReSight capability-expansion experiments, and evaluates six questions three times each over one recorded day of robot video.

**Boundary.** The integrated study reconstructs memory offline; it does not test actions changing future observations. Capability-expansion results are inherited from ReSight, not independent new experiments. Answer-time savings exclude memory construction, and scoring/input protocols differ between configurations. Reliable multi-day autonomous learning remains open.

## Exo: An Architecture for Self-Improving Systems at Runtime

**2026-10-30 · preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.00463)

**Mechanism.** Allows an agent to edit its harness and improvement procedures while working. A separate mechanism retains history and controls activation; tools, context policies, and other edits can persist into later tasks without changing model weights.

**What changes:** Agent code, Tools, Workflows. **Persistence:** both. **Learning signal:** Execution history, model cost, failures, and task feedback inform runtime code and policy revisions.

**Evaluation.** Studies open-world game objectives, AppWorld scenario variants, SREGym incidents, and a coding-task sequence. Graded-task controls share the starting policy with editing disabled.

**Boundary.** Game results use one standalone/transfer pair per objective; low-reuse quests cost more. AppWorld/SREGym transfer stays within scenarios or fault families; coding has no separate holdout. The default guardian checks builds, not correctness, and the broadly writable development configuration does not enforce the paper’s protection assumptions.

## MUSE: Multi-Level Memory with Selective Runtime Injection for Scientific Coding Agents

**2026-10-28 · preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.38332)

**Mechanism.** Builds global, approach-level, and implementation-level memories from source attempts. After offline consolidation, the banks are frozen. New tasks receive global and problem-matched guidance; an LLM gate can inject a relevant implementation lesson and check suggestion after tool interactions. Agent weights and tools stay fixed.

**What changes:** Memory, Prompts / context. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Historical task requirements, trajectories, submissions, and success/failure feedback support lesson extraction and review.

**Evaluation.** Uses shared source trajectories and disjoint test problems across PDEAgent-Bench, KernelBenchX, KernelGenBench-MS, and SWE-bench Science, with gate/level ablations and transfer between kernel benchmarks.

**Boundary.** The study uses one solving backbone and agent setup. Gate ablation changes both selection and generated advice. Memory stays frozen during testing, so results do not demonstrate continual online memory improvement. Kernel acceleration counts all test tasks that are both correct and at least 1.01 times faster, and transfer remains within related kernel tasks.

**Code / data.** [Official artifact](https://github.com/hr-jin/MUSE) — Author README documents memory components and agent callbacks; benchmark environments and verifiers are separate. Not installed or executed.

**Topics:** memory, workflows, applications, evaluation. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-11-05.

## Your Policy Is Secretly a Harness: The Decision Geometry of Agent Interfaces

**2026-10-27 · preprint · adjacent · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37255)

**Mechanism.** Decomposes regularized return into an interface-specific optimum and policy mismatch under a finite semantic-control model. It tests how presentation or execution changes can alter frozen-model behavior and how further training changes harness rankings.

**What changes:** Analysis / no retained update. **Persistence:** not-applicable. **Learning signal:** Task rewards support controlled policy training; sampled actions and stronger-teacher probes estimate deployment mismatch.

**Evaluation.** Uses exact-control MiniWoB++ experiments with six harnesses, adaptation and sampling controls, plus five coding harnesses on Terminal-Bench Lite.

**Boundary.** The theory assumes a specified KL-regularized control problem. Coding-agent ceilings are stronger-teacher proxies sampled on three tasks, not solved optima. Mismatch estimation requires substantial query budgets; observed ranking agreement does not establish universal prediction or autonomous harness optimization.

## The Right Fact, the Wrong Decision: SciValidityBench for Scientific Agent Memory

**2026-10-26 · preprint · adjacent · benchmark**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.34767)

**Mechanism.** Generates scientific histories in which a remembered fact may be invalid to use. A supplied compiler exposes decision-governing relations, separating raw records, retrieval, generic graphs, and compiled-state views.

**What changes:** Memory. **Persistence:** not-applicable. **Learning signal:** Programmatic validity oracles and paired state-changing or corruption-repair controls; no trained update loop is evaluated.

**Evaluation.** Evaluates 64 task specifications across five validity modules, six domains, and four model families, with counterfactual, repair, and serialization controls.

**Boundary.** Histories and clinical scenarios are synthetic, and compilation rules are supplied. Effects vary by reader and module; richer state sometimes hurts. Curator interpretation: this evaluates state use, not autonomous discovery of validity rules or continual learning in deployed scientists.

**Code / data.** [Official artifact](https://github.com/SciValidityBench/SciValidityBench) — Paper-linked repository and benchmark README inspected; release tests and model experiments were not run.

**Topics:** memory, evaluation, safety, applications. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-10-30.

## How Do Coding-Agent Harnesses Self-Evolve? An Empirical Study of Retrospective Adaptation

**2026-10-26 · preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.34938)

**Mechanism.** Studies individually retained harness adaptations proposed by a retrospective skill, including context instructions and known-failure files. Fresh sessions with and without each change test whether the targeted action recurs on later same-repository issues.

**What changes:** Agent code, Prompts / context. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Completed coding-session traces generate proposals; researchers select changes and define later behavioral checks.

**Evaluation.** Analyzes 125 proposals from thirty SWE-bench Verified sessions, implements twenty-four proposals, and evaluates twelve adaptations in thirteen transfer events, with five sessions per harness.

**Boundary.** Human selection and evaluation remain central. Repeated-work reduction is a behavioral proxy, not proof of better task success or lower latency. Targeted task selection, partly unblinded labeling, one agent, and small samples limit generalization; some changes add unrelated work.

## Agent Memory as Recommendation: Recommender-System Design for Long-Term Memory of LLM Agents

**2026-10-26 · preprint · adjacent · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.34673)

**Mechanism.** Retrieves a fused lexical/dense pool, ranks stored turns with a separately trained LightGBM model and fills a token budget. The serving ranker is frozen; the answering model does not learn from deployment feedback. Optional generated records add a retrieval channel and date cues.

**What changes:** Model weights. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Gold evidence-turn annotations from 152 development questions train a separate ranking model.

## Memory Tax: Dissecting the Net Value of Agent Memory

**2026-10-25 · preprint · adjacent · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.34073)

**Mechanism.** Defines memory benefit and tax as query-level gains and losses relative to raw-history RAG. Gold-evidence mapping, retrieval replay, writer–reader swaps and source-augmentation probes examine construction and access failures alongside cases where memory helps.

**What changes:** Analysis / no retained update. **Persistence:** not-applicable. **Learning signal:** Not applicable: comparative analysis of memory construction, retrieval, and downstream use.

**Evaluation.** ArXiv v1 compares eleven systems on three conversational benchmarks with three QA backbones, using stratified subsets and configuration controls. It adds fifteen-benchmark retrieval probes, six experiential task settings with frozen training-derived memory, and two video-consistency evaluations.

**Boundary.** Tax depends on the chosen RAG reference; it is not monetary cost. Retrieval scope normalizes by each store rather than equal absolute tokens. Gold mapping is imperfect, QA swaps can also change retrieval, and subsets/configurations differ. Experiential gains over RAG need not beat no memory; world-model comparisons do not isolate the memory representation.

<a id="self-evolving-continual-learners"></a>

## Are Self-Evolving Agents Continual Learners?

**2026-10-19 · preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.25858)

**Mechanism.** Evaluates frozen-model agents that update retrieved experience, a shared prompt, or harness files on drifting streams. It separates gains on current tasks from interference with unseen families and forgetting of earlier ones.

**What changes:** Memory, Prompts / context, Agent code. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Environment task-success feedback used by the evaluated evolvers; held-out checkpoint tests measure retention and interference.

**Evaluation.** ReasoningBank, GEPA, and Meta-Harness are compared with a common Gemini 3.6 Flash backbone on four streams built from BIRD, BFCL, and ScienceWorld, with disjoint held-out evaluations.

**Boundary.** Findings concern these implementations, one backbone, and constructed drift schedules. The retrieval baseline always injects its nearest memory without a similarity threshold; global edits and conflicting workflows expose different failure modes, not a universal impossibility result.

**Code / data.** Official runnable code was not independently established in this review; this does not imply that no release exists.

**Topics:** continual-learning, evaluation, memory, prompts, architecture. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-10-29.

[Source 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.25858) · [Source 2](https://arxiv.org/html/2610.25858v1)

<a id="rem-experience-memory"></a>

## REM: What to Store, When to Recall, What to Forget in Experience Memory for Coding Agents

**2026-10-19 · preprint · Author reports NeurIPS 2026 CLEA workshop acceptance; venue record not independently verified. · adjacent · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.27377)

**Mechanism.** Consolidates past coding traces into phased documents, injects a retrieved document at task start, and exposes a detailed implementation record only when the agent struggles. The detailed record is evicted after one exposure.

**What changes:** Memory, Prompts / context. **Persistence:** both. **Learning signal:** Completed trajectories supply structured experience; a hand-written in-loop struggle signal controls when detailed records enter context.

**Evaluation.** Studies 99 SWE-ContextBench Lite tasks, with three replicates for the principal Sonnet 4.5 conditions, retrieval comparisons, ablations, and additional model contrasts.

**Boundary.** Experiments reuse a fixed experience pool rather than an online-growing memory. Recall-policy contrasts do not reach p<0.05 at this sample size; several secondary conditions run once. Retrieval baselines use different configurations, and stronger agents can be harmed by memory. All tasks retrieve same-repository experience; similarity to gold patches was not measured.

**Code / data.** An official implementation was not independently verified in this review; this does not establish that none exists.

**Topics:** memory, evaluation, applications. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-10-29.

<a id="memcomposer"></a>

## MemComposer: Learning to Assemble Memories for LLM Agents via Reinforcement Learning

**2026-10-15 · preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21091)

**Mechanism.** Trains a memory-composition policy to choose the number, identity, and ordering of retrieved experiences. GRPO-based Experience Policy Optimization updates the composer while keeping the executor, retriever, and memory bank fixed.

**What changes:** Model weights, Prompts / context. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Downstream task-success rewards from complete agent interactions, plus selection-size and output-format penalties.

**Evaluation.** Reports three tau-squared-bench domains with 4B and 8B executors, memory-token costs, ordering ablations, and transfer across domains, executors, and memory sources.

**Boundary.** This is external policy training, not continual growth of the memory bank. Frontier-scale executors and non-procedural memories are untested; sequence rewards confound selection and ordering, and several per-executor performance-gap confidence intervals include zero.

**Code / data.** [Official artifact](https://github.com/Makr-Xie/MemComposer) — Author-linked public repository page inspected; not executed.

**Topics:** memory, model-training, prompts. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-10-29.

<a id="harness2"></a>

## Harness^2: Recursive Agent Harnessing for an Open World

**2026-10-09 · preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14224)

**Mechanism.** Proposes and probes harness edits on the current task, then composes a successor. Adopted harnesses and evidence-linked lessons enter a persistent library that guides later improvements; each new task starts from the common base harness.

**What changes:** Agent code, Prompts / context, Memory, Skills, Tools. **Persistence:** both. **Learning signal:** Contrasts between executions of candidate and reference harnesses, interpreted by model-based editors and reflection.

**Evaluation.** Tests WorkBuddy-Bench, JobBench, and Legal Agent Benchmark across two models and two initial harnesses, with recursion budgets, component ablations, and library-transfer analyses.

**Boundary.** Behavioral contrasts do not verify correctness and can share model biases. Stage instructions, decision rules, and model weights remain fixed while the library evolves. Extra probes incur inference cost; benchmark gains do not establish unrestricted or indefinitely improving autonomy.

**Code / data.** [Official artifact](https://github.com/google-research/harness2) — Author repository and README inspected; not installed or executed. Its documented network defaults require separate evaluation-contamination controls.

**Topics:** recursive-improvement, architecture, memory, skills, applications. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-10-30.

## EmbodiedRSI: Active Continual Robot Learning Through Hypothesis-Guided Co-Evolution

**2026-10-07 · preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.10498)

**Mechanism.** Selects informative trials over code/skill hypotheses and retains successful revisions in hierarchical memory. A PPO-trained manager learns memory actions while the robot foundation model and memory operator remain frozen during evolution.

**What changes:** Agent code, Skills, Memory, Model weights. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Matched execution outcomes, hypothesis uncertainty, experiment cost, and later improvement used to train a memory manager.

**Evaluation.** Reports RoboCasa365 and LIBERO-Pro with disjoint evolution/evaluation seeds, component ablations, and transfer of the simulation-evolved harness to five physical SO-101 tasks.

**Boundary.** “Zero-shot” concerns the harness: the real-robot SmolVLA backbone was first fine-tuned on fifty human demonstrations per task. Thirty trials per condition/task and bounded benchmarks do not establish indefinite retention or improvement of the outer selection procedure.

**Code / data.** Official runnable code was not established in this source review; nothing was installed or executed.

<a id="ascent"></a>

## ASCENT: Online Test-Time Training of Long-Horizon Agents via Self-Distillation of Verified Experience

**2026-10-04 · preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.05303)

**Mechanism.** After one scored attempt per task, a frozen copy of the initial model reads accepted experience with hindsight. Its token distributions train persistent LoRA adapters for subsequent tasks; invalid-action turns are removed from the privileged teacher input.

**What changes:** Model weights. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Completed execution trajectories accepted by an environment verifier, with action-validity feedback.

**Evaluation.** The authors report success, interaction cost, ablations, and held-out scene transfer on ALFWorld and WebShop with two model sizes, plus AppWorld experiments.

**Boundary.** The method needs an available verifier and update compute. WebShop adaptation accepts scores of at least 0.9 although reported exact success requires 1.0; outcome acceptance does not identify causally useful actions or prove a shortest solution.

**Code / data.** [Official artifact](https://github.com/artificer-ai-lab/ASCENT) — Official repository page inspected; no installation, training, or result reproduction performed.

**Topics:** model-training, continual-learning, applications. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-10-29.

<a id="verse"></a>

## VERSE: Verified Self-Evolving Optimizer for Agent Harnesses

**2026-10-02 · preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02616)

**Mechanism.** Updates an executor harness and the optimizer's own prompts, skills, tools, hooks, and notes. Verification tools test proposed fixes and diagnoses before submission while both models remain frozen.

**What changes:** Agent code, Prompts / context, Skills, Tools, Memory. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Executed draft checks, failure replay and perturbation, training regressions, and validation summaries.

**Evaluation.** Adds VERSE to four reimplemented harness optimizers, evaluating held-out SWE-rebench and newer multilingual tasks; also studies Terminal-Bench and component ablations.

**Boundary.** Selection rules and core verification tools remain fixed. Matched candidate counts do not imply equal total compute. Reimplemented baselines differ from their original systems; self-evolution benefits vary by host, and noisy outcome changes often fail to reproduce.

<a id="rifar"></a>

## RIFAR: Reliability-Informed and Forgetting-Aware Replay for Continual Robot Learning with World-Action Models

**2026-10-02 · preprint · arXiv preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.03079)

**Mechanism.** Retains short historical demonstration prefixes, generates replay trajectories and screens their action–visual consistency. After initial new-task adaptation, replay prioritizes reliable trajectories showing greater action drift. Both the policy and reliability model receive staged updates.

**What changes:** Model weights, Memory. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** New-task demonstrations, inverse-dynamics consistency of generated replay and action-prediction drift after adaptation.

**Evaluation.** Studies three LIBERO suites and a three-task Franka sequence, comparing retention, acquisition and historical-data storage with real-data and generative replay.

**Boundary.** Relies on demonstrations and fixed task sequences. The v3 reliability model learns from generated replay and can inherit its errors; rollout termination can be premature. Full real-data replay remains stronger on several metrics. Retained-history savings do not measure total training or generation cost.

**Code / data.** Official implementation availability was not established in this review; no research code was executed.

**Topics:** memory, model-training, continual-learning, applications, evaluation. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-11-09.

## Self-Evolving Defense: Continual Security Policy Learning for LLM Agents

**2026-09-29 · preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.36603)

**Mechanism.** Stores failure episodes and distills them into a hierarchical policy memory. Relevant policies condition later tasks while the acting model stays frozen.

**What changes:** Memory, Prompts / context. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** An external judge flags harmful completed trajectories; model components synthesize and organize defensive policies.

**Evaluation.** The authors evaluate eight benchmarks spanning jailbreaks, prompt injection, and coding, plus adaptive attackers and a frozen-memory control. Each benchmark starts with empty memory; updates occur only after completed episodes.

**Boundary.** The reported protocol does not establish cross-benchmark retention. Retrieval and enforcement failures remain, and learning depends on the external judge. DTap additionally uses a pre-tool guard, which must be retained when interpreting comparisons.

## Learn Now, Use Next, Trust Later: Prequential Test-Time Learning for LLM Agents

**2026-09-28 · preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.35911)

**Mechanism.** Extracts testable policy hypotheses that can guide the next decision, while keeping persistent reuse behind an evidence gate. Candidate predictions are frozen before later observations; counterevidence can withdraw promoted guidance. Model weights remain fixed.

**What changes:** Memory. **Persistence:** both. **Learning signal:** Observed action transitions and prospective checks of predicted effects in later, non-source episodes.

**Evaluation.** The paper compares two actor configurations and learning baselines across five rounds on WebArena-Lite and ALFWorld, including first-attempt analysis, safeguards ablations, and costs.

**Boundary.** Evaluation repeats tasks and excludes ten WebArena-Lite cases. Promotion relies on environment-specific evidence adapters; predictive validation does not by itself establish causal policy utility. Longer changing streams remain future work.

<a id="sage-acceptance-gate"></a>

## SAGE: A Statistical Acceptance Gate for Self-Evolving Agents

**2026-09-28 · preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.36043)

**Mechanism.** Retains skill edits only when paired wins outweigh penalized regressions, an exact binomial test rejects the null, and a regression cap is satisfied. The acting model and edit proposer remain fixed.

**What changes:** Skills. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Binary verifier outcomes for the incumbent and candidate skill on the same validation items.

**Evaluation.** Compares the gate with the same SkillOpt proposer across five benchmarks and four backbones, including component ablations and reported matched proposal/token budgets.

**Boundary.** Error control is per fixed comparison; reuse of validation data does not provide a trajectory-level guarantee. Thresholds still require held-out tuning, and tests assume binary outcomes. Multimodal and multi-agent transfer remain untested.

**Code / data.** Official implementation availability was not established in this review; no code was executed.

**Topics:** evaluation, skills, prompts. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-10-30.

<a id="reuse-evaluation"></a>

## Which Self-Improvements Should We Trust? Reliable Self-Improvement When Agents Reuse Their Benchmarks

**2026-09-27 · preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.33180)

**Mechanism.** Allocates a global error budget over possible candidate and promotion histories, accepting updates only after paired tests pass. Audit certificates stay hidden from the proposer; the paper derives simultaneous guarantees under an independent evaluation sample and decision-only feedback.

**What changes:** Model weights. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Paired incumbent-candidate scores on a protected evaluation set; only promotion decisions from that set return to the proposer.

**Evaluation.** Tests LLM-proposed classification-pipeline revisions on Covertype for 200 rounds and 30 seeds per evaluation-set size; a separate holdout estimates accepted improvements.

**Boundary.** Guarantees require bounded scores, an independent identically distributed evaluation sample, and strict feedback isolation. Experiments concern classification, and baselines are adapted styles rather than original agent systems. Finite holdout estimates are not known population truth; coding-agent and safety-metric transfer remain untested.

**Code / data.** Official runnable implementation was not verified in this review; no research code was executed.

**Topics:** evaluation, recursive-improvement, model-training. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-11-02.

## GameSmith: Scaling Zero-Sum Self-Play with Synthesised Games

**2026-09-26 · preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13995)

**Mechanism.** Synthesizes games inside fixed reward and observation templates, checks replay and independent implementations, then distills teacher trajectories into a student. Subsequent student self-play updates its weights using the Crab estimator.

**What changes:** Model weights. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Game-engine outcomes, stronger-teacher self-play traces, and a corpus-informed advantage baseline.

**Evaluation.** Reports 29 game families and 336 variants, four language-model configurations, thirteen reasoning benchmarks, corpus scaling, and matched teacher/token controls.

**Boundary.** The pipeline uses three engineered templates and a Qwen3-32B teacher. Independent implementations can share specification errors, which the manual audit observed. Transfer differs by backbone: a non-game data control performs better on Mistral. These tests do not establish indefinite self-improvement.

**Mechanism.** Converts expert self-play search into an offline corpus of action-choice traces and state questions. Supervised tuning or on-policy self-distillation transfers this information into an LLM; the LLM does not participate in expert self-play or receive search traces at inference.

## What Stops Recursive Self-Improvement in Robotics? Lessons from 123 Rounds of Agentic Skill Discovery

**2026-09-23 · preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.31760)

**Mechanism.** Coding agents revise task programs and skill implementations or request external model providers. Accepted revisions feed later rounds, while humans repair the evaluators, tests, memory machinery, and actuator descriptions.

**What changes:** Agent code, Skills, Tools. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Simulator-state diagnoses, recorded failures, replay and paired tests, and logged skill outcomes.

**Evaluation.** Reports one 123-round RoboCasa experiment over three kitchen tasks with an additional held-out task. Some local skills improve, but the target fridge task never succeeds; the record analyzes early-step bottlenecks and evaluator failures.

**Boundary.** One simulator, layout, and unreplicated run provide no matched-budget causal estimate. Human repairs and model/provider changes share the timeline. Suggested design remedies are hypotheses, and simulated skill discovery is not evidence of autonomous real-robot learning or improvement of the outer evaluation procedure.

<a id="safety-self-evolving-survey"></a>

## Safety in Self-Evolving Agents: A Survey

**2026-09-08 · preprint · core · survey**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.00093)

**Mechanism.** SAVER follows a substrate–adaptation transition through violation, exposure and response, distinguishing local utility from permission for broader reuse. It separates storage from activation, propagation from migration, and immediate containment from repair of derived memories, skills, artifacts or model state.

**What changes:** Analysis / no retained update. **Persistence:** not-applicable. **Learning signal:** Not applicable to the survey itself; it analyzes selection signals, authorization conditions and feedback that govern reusable agent-state updates.

**Evaluation.** ArXiv v1 synthesizes a scoping corpus with explicit source, deduplication and coding rules. Its benchmark tables compare observed lifecycle stages and paper-specific denominators; proposed measures cover safe promotion, boundary change, negative evidence and reactivation after repair and resumed adaptation.

**Boundary.** The 683-record inventory is not 683 independently appraised safety demonstrations: 549 classifications remain low-confidence. Screening lacks independent dual coding or preregistration, and heterogeneous results are not pooled. Proposed metrics and the conceptual authority model do not certify safety, complete recovery or the prevalence of benign adaptation drift.

**Code / data.** [Official artifact](https://github.com/xaddwell/awesome-self-evolving-agent-safety) — Author-linked survey repository and project page inspected on 2026-11-09. This artifact is a coded literature collection, not a reproduced agent defense; its corpus labels and surveyed experiments were not independently rerun.

**Topics:** surveys, safety, evaluation, memory. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-11-09.

[Source 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.00093) · [Source 2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.00093v1) · [Source 3](https://xaddwell.github.io/Awesome-Self-Evolving-Agent-Safety/) · [Source 4](https://github.com/xaddwell/awesome-self-evolving-agent-safety)

<a id="beyond-prompts-prism"></a>

## Beyond Prompts: Measuring and Optimizing LLM Tool-Agent Harnesses

**2026-09-04 · peer-reviewed · Findings of EMNLP 2026 · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.05736)

**Mechanism.** Clusters failures and routes repairs to prompts, tool-boundary middleware, or both. Evolution retains candidates on a Pareto frontier while the underlying model stays fixed.

**What changes:** Prompts / context, Agent code. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Execution failures, tool-state traces, and separate repair/gate scores before final held-out evaluation.

**Evaluation.** Compares harness optimizers on BFCL multi-round and tau2 Retail/Telecom, measuring held-out lift, repeatability, costs, and an empirical lower-tail selection metric.

**Boundary.** Telecom PRISM arms use a different scoring orchestration path from comparison arms. Lower-tail estimates are not guarantees; budgets count inner rollouts, and the study does not evaluate repeated deployment cycles or unrestricted harness rewrites.

## MASkills: Continual Skills Optimization for Multi-Agent LLM Systems

**2026-09-02 · peer-reviewed · Findings of EMNLP 2026 · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.02094)

**Mechanism.** Uses a separate critic and optimizer to refine, induce, merge, or prune persistent skill artifacts for cooperating agents. Aggregated textual feedback is smoothed across cycles; a validation gate rolls back edits that fail its acceptance threshold.

**What changes:** Skills. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Team task outcomes, LLM judgments of individual skill contributions, and validation performance.

**Evaluation.** Evaluates HotpotQA, LoCoMo, and GAIA, with transferred skill libraries, actor/topology variations, and operator ablations.

**Boundary.** Its gradient and momentum terminology describes language-space analogies, not differentiable model training. Skill attribution depends on critic judgments and researchers supply validation tasks. Benchmark transfer does not establish indefinite retention under changing deployments.

## Control-Data Flow Separation: Stable Prompt Optimization in Multi-Agent LLMs

**2026-09-01 · peer-reviewed · Findings of EMNLP 2026 · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.00621)

**Mechanism.** Keeps routing, formatting, and termination schemas outside the optimizer’s editable prompt surface. Typed validation rejects malformed control before routing while textual feedback improves task-facing prompts.

**What changes:** Prompts / context. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Task outcomes and per-example feedback on multi-agent interaction traces.

**Evaluation.** Tests BIG-Bench Hard subsets, collaborative paper-review generation, and synthetic insurance-rating workflows, with schema/retry ablations and smaller cross-model comparisons.

**Boundary.** Eventual protocol validity can include retries and does not imply correct decisions. Roles and schemas remain fixed; review quality uses an LLM judge, and additional model-family comparisons use one seed. Insurance experiments do not establish operational suitability.

<a id="memory-anchors"></a>

## Memory Anchors for Continual Robot Learning

**2026-08-27 · preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26545)

**Mechanism.** Selects old experiences near new-task observations that require conflicting actions, then enriches the replay buffer with these anchors during sequential policy training. Retention changes through both replay selection and policy updates.

**What changes:** Memory, Model weights. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Old and new task demonstrations, observation-representation overlap, and disagreement between predicted and labeled actions.

**Evaluation.** The authors test removal and enrichment of anchors on four LIBERO suites, diffusion and VLA policies, and two real-robot sequences involving jars and sweater folding, with buffer-selection ablations.

**Boundary.** Extraction requires policy latents and past training data, and recomputing their representations has a cost. Sequences contain only three to ten tasks; retention on these settings does not establish indefinite continual deployment.

**Code / data.** Official runnable code was not established in this source review; nothing was installed or executed.

**Topics:** continual-learning, memory, model-training, applications. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-10-30.

<a id="coalition-skill-reliability"></a>

## Coalition-Aware Skill Reliability for Self-Evolving Agents

**2026-08-23 · preprint · arXiv preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.22610)

**Mechanism.** Changes MemSkill's bank-admission score to include sampled joint skill effects while retaining its trained controller. Before deployment, a separate greedy procedure rebuilds target memories and masks skills whose removal improves a retrieval-quality proxy; the retained bank and mask persist.

**What changes:** Skills, Model weights. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Source outcome rewards and sampled skill-coalition knockout scores; unlabeled target-query retrieval similarity guides transfer masking.

**Evaluation.** Studies LoCoMo, LongMemEval, HotpotQA and ALFWorld with three seeds, coalition audits and six-bank target masking; the gate study covers twelve proposals.

**Boundary.** Evidence concerns one MemSkill-based setup and small banks. The highlighted target-side utility reversal has an interval including zero. Retrieval similarity is a proxy, and masking adds quadratic memory rebuild work before inference. This does not establish online adaptation to changing APIs or general skill compositions.

**Code / data.** The inspected paper promises an audit toolkit, method code and trained checkpoints; a released official implementation was not established. No code was executed.

**Topics:** skills, memory, model-training, continual-learning, evaluation. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-11-07.

## When Not to Imitate: Boundary-Aware Skill Memory for Reliable Tool-Use LLM Agents

**2026-08-23 · peer-reviewed · Findings of EMNLP 2026 · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.22339)

**Mechanism.** Builds a reusable skill library with explicit conditions, risk cues and avoidance rules. Retrieval exposes relevant boundaries under a context budget; runtime checks can block or revise tool calls, with local repair hints after failures. Model weights remain fixed.

**What changes:** Skills, Memory. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Offline successful trajectories and nearby failures supply procedures, applicability conditions and recovery notes.

**Evaluation.** Tests BFCL, AppWorld and AgentDojo across four model scales, with tool-choice probes, boundary-attention interventions and component controls.

**Boundary.** Library construction is offline, and structural validation does not certify boundary semantics. Safety and utility differ: Qwen3-8B's AgentDojo utility remains below the memory-free baseline despite lower attack success. Dynamic API changes and long-running delayed feedback are untested.

## CIDER: Continual Interactive Distillation for Embodied Reinforcement Learning

**2026-08-22 · preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.21899)

**Mechanism.** Interleaves online actor-critic learning with distillation from the preceding consolidated policy. Gradient routing separates acquisition and retention updates while producing one shared actor; historical states support distillation rather than old-task Bellman updates.

**What changes:** Model weights. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Current-task rewards, human demonstrations and corrective interventions, plus a frozen prior actor’s action distributions on archived states.

**Evaluation.** Reports sequential acquisition and retention across six real-robot household and industrial manipulation tasks, with evaluation after each stage and gradient-routing, initialization, and sampling ablations.

**Boundary.** This is human-assisted, reward-driven acquisition on short-horizon tasks. Longer tasks with sparse rewards or delayed failures may need additional supervision; the six-task result does not establish unbounded skill accumulation.

**Code / data.** Official runnable code was not established in this source review; nothing was installed or executed.

## Phantom Gains: Auditing Self-Improvement Against a Measured Null

**2026-08-20 · preprint · adjacent · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.20290)

**Mechanism.** Measures apparent per-problem changes in frozen-model controls before interpreting changes after self-training. It uses sampled solve rates, a hysteresis-based transition ledger and per-problem exact tests against pooled baseline evaluations with multiple-testing control.

**What changes:** Analysis / no retained update. **Persistence:** not-applicable. **Learning signal:** Not applicable: analysis or evaluation resource.

**Evaluation.** ArXiv v1 audits three-round Qwen3-8B LoRA training using ground-truth filtering, majority-vote SFT, a policy-gradient variant and external distillation. MATH/AIME experiments examine decoding noise, truncation, seed variation, expansion statistics and small out-of-domain probes.

**Boundary.** The strong contrast concerns twenty-two rarely reached AIME problems; the ten never reached in the pooled baseline remain inconclusive. Short adapted training protocols, one model family and an enriched MATH difficulty band limit generalization. Safety-probe power is not a confidence bound on possible harm; raw generations were not independently regraded.

## HyperSkill: Self-Evolving LLM Agents via Hypergraph-Structured Skill Memory

**2026-08-17 · preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.16114)

**Mechanism.** Stores task decompositions and reusable natural-language skills in trajectory hyperedges. Task-level and subtask-level retrieval select lessons, while co-occurrence ranks skills. With fixed model weights, outcome-weighted pruning and merging maintain the graph after episodes; retrieved context stays fixed within an episode.

**What changes:** Skills, Memory. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Ground-truth task outcomes and execution length update skill utility in the main experiments; a separate variant uses self-judged outcomes.

**Evaluation.** ArXiv v1 compares ten adapted memory baselines on 100 xBench, 165 GAIA and 170 WebWalkerQA tasks using two backbones in a fixed sequential order. It studies retrieval/structure ablations, maintenance settings, cost, graph growth and ground-truth versus self-judged feedback.

**Boundary.** Single-order cumulative curves do not establish causal compounding or long-term retention. Retrieval budgets differ from baselines and the flat-memory ablation changes multiple components. Headline gains are against no memory, with ties to some stronger baselines. Self-judging lowers scores, latency can rise, and some prose/figure descriptions disagree.

**Code / data.** [Official artifact](https://github.com/rux001/HyperSkill) — Official paper-linked repository and setup/runner README inspected on 2026-11-09; no code, models or benchmark data executed or downloaded. Source availability is not an independent reproduction.

**Topics:** skills, memory. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-11-09.

<a id="hierarchical-self-improvement"></a>

## Hierarchical Self-Improvement: A Framework for Task-Specific Evolvable Agent Harnesses

**2026-08-09 · preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.08466)

**Mechanism.** Uses one frozen model in separate task, evolver and meta-evolver contexts. The evolver rewrites a task-family harness; the meta-evolver edits its search strategy. Version archives and lessons persist across five outer iterations. The implemented terminal selector is described as fixed in the appendix and README, despite broader main-text wording.

**What changes:** Agent code, Workflows. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Benchmark progress, development/validation feedback, committed-version history and stored lessons guide harness and evolution-strategy edits; evaluator and outer execution anchor are fixed.

**Evaluation.** ArXiv v1 compares initial, meta-off and meta-on harnesses on BALROG with DeepSeek-V4-Flash. Five suites reuse task families with new episode seeds; three BabaIsAI sub-suites use held-out tasks. It reports progress scores, limited evaluation repeats and qualitative evolution histories, including near-zero NLE results.

**Boundary.** One backbone and short runs do not establish an intrinsic capability ceiling. Task-time thinking flags do not equate total computation, and no matched-cost search baseline is reported. Meta-evolution is not uniformly better on held-out tasks. Protocol descriptions and uncertainty denominators differ between sections; cross-family transfer and indefinite retention remain untested.

**Code / data.** [Official artifact](https://github.com/TailinZhou/hsi) — Official repository README, pipeline, configuration and result descriptions inspected on 2026-11-09; no benchmark, model or research code executed. Current documentation does not independently establish the paper experiments or enforcement of scope isolation.

## EvolveNet: Collaborative Harness Evolution for Agent Self-Improvement

**2026-08-05 · preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.04968)

**Mechanism.** Clients modify a shared executable harness using frozen models; a server integrates globally useful and domain-conditional edits, validates the merge, and redistributes it. The fixed outer procedure permits one revision before rollback; binary validation accepts equal aggregate accuracy even when individual tasks regress.

**What changes:** Agent code, Workflows. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Labeled local task outcomes, full execution traces and separate server-validation feedback guide proposals, scoped merging and adoption.

**Evaluation.** ArXiv v3 runs three evolution rounds on five benchmark subsets, with 30–200 held-out items each. It compares selection, centralized search and fixed-client aggregation variants, then analyzes retained client gains, search cost, a second BIRD model stack and conditional composition bounds.

**Boundary.** Confirmation settings and merger replays use single realizations. Matched proposer counts exclude added aggregation cost; end-to-end BIRD runtime is longer than centralized baselines. Validation is repeatedly reused, scope isolation is assumed rather than certified, and last-round gain retention is not lifelong non-forgetting. Full traces are shared, so no privacy guarantee follows.

**Code / data.** [Official artifact](https://github.com/junnie00/EvolveNet) — Official paper-linked repository and release/setup README inspected on 2026-11-09; no code, models or benchmarks run. The release documents four benchmark implementations and excludes original response caches/results; the five-setting paper is not independently reproduced.

**Topics:** architecture, workflows, continual-learning. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-11-09.

<a id="agentstream"></a>

## AgentStream: How Well Do Self-Evolving LLM Agents Perform Under Streaming Tasks?

**2026-07-31 · preprint · core · benchmark**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.00155)

**Mechanism.** Carries prompts, memories, skills or a custom harness between tasks with frozen foundation-model weights. Isolated streams maintain separate state, Sequential carries it across one domain order, and Interleaved mixes domains. Adapted methods use execution observations and self-generated feedback without test labels.

**What changes:** Memory, Skills, Prompts / context, Workflows. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Execution outcomes and model-generated feedback; ground-truth test labels are withheld from adaptation.

**Evaluation.** Full v2 crosses five adapted methods with three models and six benchmarks, using 50 fixed tasks per benchmark and three arrival-order seeds. It reports native task scores, per-seed results, cumulative curves, state/update counts and a separate single-evaluation cost analysis for two models.

**Boundary.** Model capability is specific to the selected harness, tasks and reasoning settings; it is not an experimentally isolated causal variable. Sequential tests one domain order and does not revisit old tasks to measure forgetting. Small aggregate differences and large task-level variance limit universal method rankings. Cost results use one evaluation and can accompany regressions.

**Code / data.** [Official artifact](https://github.com/microsoft/Sico/tree/main/labs/AgentStream) — Full 43-page arXiv v2, substantive Appendices A–E, complete prompts, all plots and per-seed tables read on 2026-11-09. ## Self-Improvements in Modern Agentic Systems: A Survey

**2026-07-14 · preprint · core · survey**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.13104)

**Mechanism.** Models the agent as foundation-model parameters plus a persistent scaffold of prompts, memory, tools and control logic, distinct from ephemeral execution state. It distinguishes behavior-generated training signals consumed by an optimizer from direct scaffold edits, and treats skills as reusable updates across these substrates.

**What changes:** Analysis / no retained update. **Persistence:** not-applicable. **Learning signal:** Not applicable to the survey itself; it separates self-generated demonstrations, evaluative feedback and exploratory experience from the model or scaffold component updated.

**Evaluation.** ArXiv v1 reviews historical foundations, model/scaffold methods and six application domains. It supplies qualitative memory comparison tables and a paper–benchmark usage matrix, then proposes budgeted learning trajectories, held-out transfer, old-task regressions, judge calibration and separate evaluation-cost reporting.

**Boundary.** The formal update equations and verifier gates are an organizing framework, not proofs of safe or monotonic improvement. Qualitative ratings and benchmark incidence are not measured effect sizes. Some included systems do not evolve their own improver or retain changes across tasks; scaffold edits can still forget useful state. No reproducible corpus-screening protocol is provided.

The artifact is a literature hub; no listed implementation, historical system or benchmark was independently executed for this review.

## PACE: Anytime-Valid Acceptance Tests for Self-Evolving Agents

**2026-06-06 · preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.08106)

**Mechanism.** Places a sequential statistical gate between proposed prompt edits and retention. A betting-based evidence process accepts an edit only after its paired outcomes cross a threshold; otherwise the incumbent remains.

**What changes:** Prompts / context. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Paired candidate/incumbent correctness on development instances.

**Evaluation.** Author experiments use Qwen2.5 prompt evolution on GSM8K, SVAMP, and ARC-Challenge, with planted-gain and stochastic regimes and a separate audit pool. Statistical gates reduce noisy commitments relative to greedy selection.

**Boundary.** The guarantee is per candidate under a conditional paired-null assumption, not a guarantee for the whole adaptive search. Experiments cover one model family and prompt edits; the finite audit and development-set coverage limit interpretation. Small genuine gains may be rejected.

<a id="self-evolution-generalization-gap"></a>

## On the Generalization Gap in Self-Evolving Language Model Reasoning

**2026-05-31 · peer-reviewed · ICML 2026 · adjacent · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.01075)

**Mechanism.** Compares single-round verification, feedback-guided revision, repeated preference training, and curricula inside a controlled generator-verifier loop. Retained changes are trained policy weights rather than an evolving agent harness.

**What changes:** Model weights. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Preference labels and revision feedback generated by the same base model from supplied unlabeled prompts; oracle labels form comparison arms.

**Evaluation.** Studies easy-to-hard Knights and Knaves reasoning and OpenThoughts-based training with mathematical/generalization tests. Gains often plateau below oracle supervision; a larger-model revision condition nearly closes the gap.

**Boundary.** The restricted offline setup is not an impossibility result for all self-improvement. Open-ended tests cannot isolate verifier error from prompt-distribution shifts, and online-RL comparison rows use different starting models and supervision. Improved pass@1 with nearly unchanged pass@32 limits claims about expanded solution coverage.

**Code / data.** Official runnable code was not independently verified in this review; no research implementation was executed.

<a id="muse-autoskill"></a>

## MUSE-Autoskill: Self-Evolving Agents via Skill Creation, Memory, Management, and Evaluation

**2026-05-26 · preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.27366)

**Mechanism.** A fixed-weight agent creates and maintains portable skill packages with optional scripts/tests, per-skill experience and shared memory. Catalog-guided loading and context compression support reuse; checks can trigger package edits. Most observed generated packages are textual procedures rather than tested code.

**What changes:** Skills, Memory. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Source trajectories, generated tests when present, runtime checks and per-skill notes guide skill creation/refinement; a separate sequential-memory diagnostic supplies verifier feedback.

**Evaluation.** ArXiv v2 compares four GPT-5.5-backed runtimes on 75 SkillsBench tasks with five runs each and 100 SkillLearnBench instances. It separates same-task skill re-evaluation, transfer to Hermes, coverage/cost diagnostics and a task-sequential memory-on/off experiment with two-pass verifier feedback.

**Boundary.** The 85.24% result covers only 47 successfully generated-skill tasks; all-task self-created performance is 53.42%, below human skills at 59.67%. Source and reuse tasks coincide, and transfer changes runtime rather than backbone. Only 8% of MUSE packages contain tests. Restricted coverage, brittle skills and incomplete cost traces limit generalization.

**Code / data.** Code availability not verified in this review.

**Topics:** skills, memory, evaluation. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-11-09.

## SkillOpt: Executive Strategy for Self-Evolving Agent Skills

**2026-05-22 · preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.23904)

**Mechanism.** An external optimizer revises one skill document through bounded edits, rejected-edit memory, and slow epoch-level updates. The target model and execution harness stay fixed; a selected text artifact is reused on later tasks.

**What changes:** Skills, Prompts / context. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Scored task rollouts, optimizer-model critiques, and separate selection-set scores gate retained text edits.

**Evaluation.** Reports six benchmarks, seven target models, and direct-chat/Codex/Claude Code settings, plus component, budget, and nearby model/harness/task-transfer comparisons.

**Boundary.** Requires reliable scoring and selection data plus substantial optimization calls. Zero extra deployment model calls does not mean zero training cost. A single skill can be insufficient for heterogeneous domains, and near-domain transfer is not unrestricted continual improvement.

## LongMemEval-V2: Evaluating Long-Term Agent Memory Toward Experienced Colleagues

**2026-05-12 · preprint · adjacent · benchmark**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.12493)

**Mechanism.** Streams stored web-agent trajectories into memory and asks the system to return bounded evidence for a fixed reader. AgentRunbook-R indexes state slices, transitions and procedural notes; AgentRunbook-C uses a coding agent to inspect trajectory files with manifests and helper tools.

**What changes:** Memory. **Persistence:** not-applicable. **Learning signal:** Not applicable: analysis or evaluation resource.

**Evaluation.** ArXiv v1 evaluates 451 human-curated questions across four customized websites and five memory abilities, using 100-trajectory and roughly 500-trajectory histories. It reports fixed-reader QA, query latency, paired-bootstrap comparisons, pool/scaffold ablations and error analysis.

**Boundary.** This evaluates pre-collected evidence gathering, not live task execution or lifelong retention. RAG and coding-agent controllers differ, query latency excludes the full ingestion cost, and gains are not uniform across categories. Question filtering, reader prompting and semantic-judge rules shape the measured accuracy.

## MEMOREPAIR: Barrier-First Cascade Repair in Agentic Memory

**2026-05-08 · preprint · arXiv preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.07242)

**Mechanism.** Withdraws an invalidated artifact's recorded descendants before repair, rebuilds successors from retained support, and republishes only validated dependency-closed selections. A fixed cost–value tradeoff reduces selection to a min-cut; optional neural-artifact repairs use supplied unlearning operators.

**What changes:** Memory, Skills, Model weights. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Explicit deletion, correction or interface-migration events, recorded dependencies and artifact-specific validation.

**Evaluation.** Uses ToolBench/StableToolBench and MemoryArena traces to compare stale exposure, successor recovery and repair cost, including a ToolLLaMA adapter repair study.

**Boundary.** Isolation assumes complete influence provenance and adequate validators; missing edges can leave stale descendants visible. The reported task diagnostic is constructed from repair/exposure sets, not native end-to-end task success. Costs exclude the withdrawal barrier, and parameter erasure is not guaranteed.

**Code / data.** Official implementation availability was not established in this review; no code was executed.

**Topics:** memory, skills, continual-learning, safety, evaluation. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-11-07.

## SkillFlow:Benchmarking Lifelong Skill Discovery and Evolution for Autonomous Agents

**2026-04-19 · preprint · core · benchmark**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.17308)

**Mechanism.** Starts each workflow family with an empty skill library, solves its tasks in difficulty order, and carries additions, revisions and deletions to subsequent tasks. Library state resets between families; the execution models are not weight-trained. Skill use is detected through reads or calls of stored files.

**What changes:** Skills. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Completed-task trajectories and externally supplied verifier-derived rubrics drive a fixed prompt that generates skill-file patches.

**Evaluation.** ArXiv v1 constructs 166 tasks in twenty families with common workflow structure, model-assisted generation and human review. Eleven model/native-harness combinations compare vanilla execution with skill evolution, including family-level outcomes, library growth, cost and an Opus raw-history control.

**Boundary.** This tests short related-task curricula, not retention across interleaved task families. Native harnesses differ and repeated-run/order uncertainty is not reported. High skill usage can accompany regression. The raw-history control has inconsistent reported values, and appendix verifier-toolchain failures complicate attribution of some errors.

**2026-04-18 · peer-reviewed · Findings of ACL 2026 · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.16968)

**Mechanism.** Studies safety changes when offline Agent Workflow Memory or online ReasoningBank supplies accumulated experience to frozen models. Varying experience size and a length-matched prompt control probe the contribution of retrieved content.

**What changes:** Memory. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Benign execution experience and, in mixed-stream experiments, execution or refusal experiences retained by the evaluated frameworks.
