## Hyperagents

**2026-03-19 · preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.19461)

**Mechanism.** An editable Python program contains both the task agent and the meta agent that modifies it. Prompts, tools, parsing, memory and modification logic can persist across generations. A separate pilot also permits changes to parent selection.

**What changes:** Agent code, Workflows, Memory. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Task outcomes and archived evaluation traces guide self-edits. Validation scores select agents where available; the main evaluator, task data, foundation models and parent-selection rule stay fixed.

**Evaluation.** ArXiv v2 studies coding, acceptance prediction, simulated robot reward design and math grading over five runs. Transferring only the meta agent recovers nearly all combined-transfer benefit in a 50-iteration math-grading test; continued-transfer and parent-selection comparisons include nonsignificant differences.

**Boundary.** Initial zero scores partly reflect malformed output. Acceptance prediction is not review quality; robotics uses one simulated robot with two objectives. Full math-benchmark results include training/validation items, and coding subset descriptions differ. Transfer supports reusable improvement code, not unbounded acceleration; iteration counts do not equal compute budgets.

## Benchmarking Agent Memory in Interdependent Multi-Session Agentic Tasks

**2026-02-18 · peer-reviewed · ICML 2026 · core · benchmark**

[Primary source](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v306/he26am.html)

**Mechanism.** Constructs shopping, travel, search and research-reasoning task chains, comparing verbatim history, retrieval stores and external memory systems. Memory resets between overall tasks and persists across their subtasks; the reported implementation primarily retrieves once per session.

**What changes:** Memory, Skills. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Earlier subtask actions and observations update episode-local persistent memory for later dependent sessions. The released formal-reasoning setup keeps model-judge outcomes out of memory by default.

**Evaluation.** The final ICML paper reports 701 tasks and 4,850 subtasks, completion/progress and latency metrics, an additional task backbone, conditional dependency-depth analysis and oracle-like injection of prior outcomes plus distilled workflows.

**Boundary.** Failures combine memory, reasoning, planning and tool use. Search/formal success scores the final subtask, unlike all-constraint shopping/travel success. Benefits and latency vary by backend and domain; prose, table aggregates and some case labels disagree. Oracle-like memory is approximate, and formal results use model judging rather than certified proofs.

**Code / data.** [Official artifact](https://github.com/ZexueHe/MemoryArena) — Official preview README and formal-reasoning/search setup documentation inspected on 2026-11-09. They document separate memory/environment services, model-based grading and local search indexes; current release settings are not a verified paper reproduction. No code, services, models or datasets installed or executed.

**Topics:** memory, continual-learning, evaluation, applications. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-11-09.

<a id="skillrl"></a>

## SkillRL: Evolving Agents via Recursive Skill-Augmented Reinforcement Learning

**2026-02-09 · peer-reviewed · NeurIPS 2026 · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.08234)

**Mechanism.** A teacher distills successes and failures into general and task-specific skills and generates a cold-start SFT dataset. GRPO then updates the acting policy while validation failures trigger skill additions. The policy and skill bank persist; the teacher, update procedure and optimizer remain fixed.

**What changes:** Skills, Model weights. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Task rewards, teacher-generated skill distillation, and validation failures.

**Evaluation.** Full v2 covers ALFWorld, WebShop and seven search QA datasets, component ablations, teacher-versus-self-distillation controls, validation curves and skill examples. The main Qwen2.5-7B setup uses o3; a stronger Kimi model is also tested with self-distillation. Several comparison rows come from prior reports.

**Boundary.** Teacher-generated SFT and skill guidance jointly change the training pipeline, so gains over vanilla RL do not isolate abstraction alone. Validation failures are learning inputs. No error bars are reported, and benefits are not uniform across task categories or QA datasets. The measured full-prompt reduction is about 10%, distinct from the larger skill-compression claim.

**Code / data.** [Official artifact](https://github.com/aiming-lab/SkillRL) — Full 31-page arXiv v2, substantive Appendices A–F, checklist and all figures/tables/cases read on 2026-11-09; official NeurIPS poster record verifies acceptance. README at 4d984d4 documents template and embedding retrieval modes whose defaults differ from the paper description. Code/checkpoint links were inspected, not installed, downloaded or executed.

**Topics:** skills, memory, model-training. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-11-09.

<a id="group-evolving-agents"></a>

## Group-Evolving Agents: Open-Ended Self-Improvement via Experience Sharing

**2026-02-04 · peer-reviewed · COLM 2026 · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.04837)

**Mechanism.** Selects pairs of agents using performance and behavioral novelty, shares their experience, and generates framework-level patches for both. A fixed reflection/evolution/archive procedure retains usable variants; the coding models are not weight-trained.

**What changes:** Agent code, Workflows. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Task-success patterns, shared framework patches, failed-task traces and evaluation outcomes guide parent selection and offspring edits.

**Evaluation.** ArXiv v1 compares staged SWE-bench/Polyglot evaluations against a DGM-style baseline with matched offspring counts and model schedules, then tests a selected agent across backbones. Five injected-bug trials supply the faulty agent with a bug-free peer.

**Boundary.** Matched agent counts do not establish equal token cost. Polyglot uses small subsets, while human-framework comparisons use different models/protocols. The 88.3% headline and 88.0% transfer figure are unreconciled. Bug-repair results compare group and individual iterations, not a common compute unit.

**Code / data.** Official code availability was not established in this source review.

**Topics:** architecture, recursive-improvement, applications. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-11-09.

## TAME: A Trustworthy Test-Time Evolution of Agent Memory with Systematic Benchmarking

**2026-02-03 · peer-reviewed · EMNLP 2026 · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.03224)

**Mechanism.** An executor retrieves useful experiences with risk guidance from a shared memory bank. An evaluator revises reuse priorities after outcomes, while new experiences enter with trust annotations; model weights remain fixed.

**What changes:** Memory. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Accurate binary task-outcome feedback, evaluator judgments of memory contribution, and model-generated trust annotations.

**Evaluation.** Trust-Memevo evolves initially empty memory on benign science, math, tool-use, and coding streams using two backbones, then freezes memory for separate trustworthiness tests.

**Boundary.** The inspected v2 uses a shared bank, differing from the initial dual-memory description. Aggregate trust scores need not reflect every safety dimension. Evaluation is text-only, and accurate outcome feedback is supplied; this does not certify safe open-ended adaptation.

## Reasoning Cache: Continual Improvement Over Long Horizons via Short-Horizon RL

**2026-02-03 · peer-reviewed · ICML 2026 · adjacent · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.03773)

**Mechanism.** Alternates bounded reasoning attempts with summary updates for the same problem. GRPO trains summary-conditioned generation, and a replay buffer supplies later-turn summaries; inference expands the reasoning budget without updating weights.

**What changes:** Model weights, Memory. **Persistence:** both. **Learning signal:** Correctness rewards on supplied mathematical prompt-answer pairs, with generated reasoning summaries reused during training.

**Evaluation.** Tests mathematical benchmarks and FrontierScience, budget extrapolation, summary/replay ablations, and integration with other inference scaffolds. The main trained model uses a two-stage mathematics curriculum.

**Boundary.** Continual improvement here is longer within-problem inference, not persistent deployment learning. Myopic rewards can miss exploration useful only later, and summarization quality depends on the backbone. Version 2 changes IMO-AnswerBench grading after the earlier parser rejected valid answers.

## MemSkill: Learning and Evolving Memory Skills for Self-Evolving Agents

**2026-02-02 · peer-reviewed · NeurIPS 2026 · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.02474)

**Mechanism.** PPO trains a lightweight controller to select memory skills for a fixed LLM executor. A fixed designer revises INSERT/UPDATE guidance from labeled hard cases; DELETE/NOOP primitives remain fixed in the supplied prompt. Skill-bank rollback uses late-cycle training rewards. Trace-specific memories and reusable memory skills are separate stores.

**What changes:** Model weights, Skills, Memory. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Downstream F1 or task success trains a separate skill-selection controller; hard training cases guide LLM-authored skill revisions.

**Evaluation.** Full November 2026 v3 covers conversational QA, offline-experience ALFWorld, HotpotQA and added AppWorld/smaller-model comparisons, including demonstration-free and alternative-selector controls. LoCoMo uses a 6/2/2 conversation split; LongMemEval transfer uses validation tuning and a roughly 100-question test subset.

**Boundary.** Abstention/adversarial queries are excluded and repeated-run uncertainty is not reported. ALFWorld uses expert experience; main interactive results also include demonstrations. Higher success does not always reduce execution steps. Inference-cost savings exclude substantial API-heavy controller/skill preparation. Benchmark transfer does not establish continual deployment or privacy guarantees.

## Large Language Model Agents Are Not Always Faithful Self-Evolvers

**2026-01-30 · peer-reviewed · ICML 2026 · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v306/zhao26aw.html)

**Mechanism.** Perturbs raw trajectories and condensed memories through removal, shuffling, corruption and replacement while keeping backbone weights fixed. Outcome sensitivity and final-turn gradient attribution probe whether experience influences an agent, rather than proposing a new learning algorithm.

**What changes:** Analysis / no retained update. **Persistence:** not-applicable. **Learning signal:** Not applicable: analysis or evaluation resource.

**Evaluation.** The ICML paper studies ExpeL, Dynamic Cheatsheet, ReasoningBank and G-Memory across selected combinations of thirteen backbones and nine benchmark families, with two additional multihop-QA probes. Raw-trajectory perturbations often hurt interactive tasks more than condensed-memory changes.

**Boundary.** Aggregate success-rate stability does not prove unchanged decisions or semantic non-use. Perturbations can be visibly irrelevant, task dependence is substantial, and repeated-run uncertainty is not reported. The appendix uses embedding-gradient norms as an attribution approximation, not a causal mechanism demonstration.

## Meta Context Engineering via Agentic Skill Evolution

**2026-01-29 · peer-reviewed · ICML 2026 · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.21557)

**Mechanism.** A meta agent revises context-engineering skills, and a base agent executes them to build context files and retrieval code. A fixed history-informed evolutionary loop retains the better validation-scoring context. The reported generator uses a one-shot query-to-context interface.

**What changes:** Prompts / context, Skills, Agent code. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Labeled training rollouts and validation utility guide context revisions and skill selection. Files preserve earlier skills, context functions and evaluation history; models remain frozen.

**Evaluation.** The final ICML paper evaluates small task subsets in finance, chemistry, symptom classification, legal charge prediction and safety classification. It includes three-dataset strong-to-weak context transfer, FiNER ablations and training-efficiency comparisons, plus a separate sequential online setting.

**Boundary.** Online experiments use fixed or absent skills, not iterative skill evolution; the skill-free variant wins on three of five online tasks. Relative-gain averages are sensitive to low baselines. No repeated-run uncertainty is reported, and selected task subsets do not establish clinical, legal or general safety validity.

## Dr. Zero: Self-Evolving Search Agents without Training Data

**2026-01-11 · peer-reviewed · COLM 2026 · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.07055)

**Mechanism.** Alternately trains a search-enabled question proposer and solver. Hop-grouped relative policy optimization normalizes proposer rewards across structurally similar questions, while GRPO trains the solver on generated QA. Model weights persist; the search corpus, retriever, prompts and reward design are externally supplied.

**What changes:** Model weights. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Solver exact matches against proposer-written answers supply difficulty and outcome rewards; seed passages and retrieved Wikipedia text ground generation without independently validating every answer.

**Evaluation.** ArXiv v2 compares 3B and 7B agents on seven short-answer QA benchmarks, with three-round dynamics, hop-mixture and reward ablations, repeated-evaluation summaries and a measured proposer-compute comparison. It reports competitive, but slightly lower average scores than supervised Search-R1.

**Boundary.** The 7B model declines in round three. Intended hop counts and matching generated labels do not certify factual correctness; a supplied question has a false premise. Reported uncertainty lacks some statistical details. Efficiency measurements concern proposer training, and QA results do not establish reliable long-form research, citation fidelity or indefinite improvement.

**Code / data.** [Official artifact](https://github.com/facebookresearch/drzero) — Official paper-linked README inspected on 2026-11-09; no index, model, data or training execution. Documentation requires a Wikipedia retrieval environment. Source availability is not independent reproduction.

## AgentDevel: Reframing Self-Evolving LLM Agents as Release Engineering

**2026-01-08 · preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.04620)

**Mechanism.** A fixed development engine generates diagnostic scripts and one prompt/code/tool-wrapper release candidate per iteration. A configurable regression gate retains accepted blueprints; the same development set drives diagnosis, promotion and stopping.

**What changes:** Agent code, Workflows. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Programmatic scores or an implementation-blind LLM critic, trace-derived symptoms, and development-set pass-to-fail/fail-to-pass changes.

**Evaluation.** Reports improvements over an initial blueprint on SWE-bench Lite/Verified, WebArena and StableToolBench. Its WebArena ablation reduces regressions with gating while the ungated variant has a slightly higher final test score; cited external baselines were not rerun.

**Boundary.** No non-regression guarantee: accepted releases can still break cases, and gate thresholds, split sizes and repeated-run uncertainty are insufficiently specified. WebArena final scores differ between Table 1 (35.5) and Table 3 (34.2) without an explicit reconciliation. The test set is described as final-only, but iterative development reuses its training cases.

**Code / data.** Official code availability was not established in this source review.

## MemRL: Self-Evolving Agents via Runtime Reinforcement Learning on Episodic Memory

**2026-01-06 · preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.03192)

**Mechanism.** Keeps model weights fixed and stores intent, experience and utility triplets. Similarity filtering precedes utility-weighted ranking; a constant-step moving average updates the retrieved memories using the same outcome, and the memory bank expands.

**What changes:** Memory. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Environment or benchmark outcome rewards update scalar utility estimates for retrieved experiences, while an LLM summarizes new episodes.

**Evaluation.** ArXiv v2 separates ten-epoch repeated-task learning on HLE, BigCodeBench, ALFWorld and Lifelong Agent Bench from frozen-memory transfer on non-HLE splits. It includes retrieval ablations, cross-model memory reuse, two-domain merging, cost analysis and conditional estimator theory.

**Boundary.** HLE gains reflect repeated-question memorization, not held-out HLE generalization. At-least-once success is distinct from retained performance. Split-size reporting and validation selection need care; stationary-reward estimates do not prove absence of forgetting in an expanding memory system. Multi-memory credit assignment and false feedback remain unresolved.

**Code / data.** [Official artifact](https://github.com/MemTensor/MemRL) — Official repository linked and its public page inspected; not executed.

**Topics:** memory, continual-learning. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-11-09.

## Agentic Memory: Learning Unified Long-Term and Short-Term Memory Management for Large Language Model Agents

**2026-01-05 · peer-reviewed · ACL 2026 · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.01885)

**Mechanism.** Uses RL to train a language-model policy over six fixed long- and short-term memory operations. A three-stage curriculum creates memories, distracts the agent after resetting context, and asks a downstream question. Learned policy weights transfer across tasks; the training memory store resets between rollouts.

**What changes:** Model weights, Memory, Prompts / context. **Persistence:** both. **Learning signal:** A composite terminal reward combines graded task success, memory quality judged against reference information, and context-management proxies; the same group-normalized advantage is applied across steps.

**Evaluation.** HotpotQA training transfers to four other benchmarks using two Qwen backbones. Appendix controls add comparable short-term tools and RL to earlier memory methods. Reported averages mix success, progress and graded-answer metrics; context-length and memory-quality ablations complement task scores.

**Boundary.** Operation-count and keyword-preservation rewards are proxies, not direct measures of useful maintenance or long-term retention. Terminal credit is not causal attribution to individual edits. Full lifecycle cost, repeated-training uncertainty and indefinite shared-memory retention are not established.

<a id="memevolve"></a>

## MemEvolve: Meta-Evolution of Agent Memory Systems

**2025-12-21 · peer-reviewed · ICML 2026 · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.18746)

**Mechanism.** Evolves implementations of encoding, storage, retrieval and memory management inside a supplied interface. Candidate memory starts empty each outer iteration; selected architecture code persists. The foundation model, selection rule and redesign procedure remain fixed.

**What changes:** Memory, Agent code. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Trajectory outcomes, API cost and latency guide fixed Pareto selection and diagnose-and-design prompts. Each candidate also builds experience while processing its task stream.

**Evaluation.** The final ICML paper adds component ablations, three-run evaluations, random/greedy search controls and a five-round extension. TaskCraft-evolved architectures transfer to WebWalkerQA, xBench, new backbones and agent frameworks; the principal GAIA evaluation also uses GAIA Level-1 tasks during evolution.

**Boundary.** GAIA aggregate performance is not wholly held out from architecture search. Reported pass@1–3 rows mix budgets and models; per-query API cost excludes full search amortization, and latency exceeds the memory-free baseline. Repeated evaluation does not establish independent search-run robustness or unbounded meta-improvement.

**Code / data.** [Official artifact](https://github.com/bingreeky/MemEvolve) — Official EvolveLab/MemEvolve README inspected on 2026-11-09. It documents Python/API setup and a checkpointed tournament CLI, but labels the release unfinished; current defaults and method inventory differ from the final paper. No installation, model calls or benchmark execution performed.

**Topics:** memory, architecture, recursive-improvement, evaluation. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-11-09.

## Agent0: Unleashing Self-Evolving Agents from Zero Data via Tool-Integrated Reasoning

**2025-11-20 · peer-reviewed · COLM 2026 · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.16043)

**Mechanism.** Alternates curriculum-agent GRPO training with executor updates on filtered generated tasks. The executor interleaves reasoning and Python calls; ADPO scales advantages and adjusts clipping using answer consistency. Both models change within a fixed procedure.

**What changes:** Model weights. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Curriculum rewards combine answer self-consistency, capped tool-response counts and repetition penalties. Executor rewards match majority-vote pseudo-labels; code execution supplies intermediate feedback but does not independently certify those labels.

**Evaluation.** Two Qwen base sizes are evaluated across seven math and three general-reasoning benchmarks over three iterations. Controls include tool access, curriculum training, ADPO and interaction turns. AMC/AIME use mean accuracy over 32 samples; other benchmarks use greedy pass@1.

**Boundary.** Pretraining, prompts, rewards and tool infrastructure remain supplied. Consensus and tool frequency are not correctness guarantees; some illustrated tasks are ill-posed. Headline gains are relative percentages, and aggregate definitions differ across tables. Peak scores, limited repeats and unequal budgets constrain broader generalization.

**Code / data.** [Official artifact](https://github.com/aiming-lab/Agent0) — Official series and Agent0 study READMEs inspected on 2026-11-09. The language and vision-language studies are separate; setup documents sandbox services and manual checkpoint selection between iterations. No installation, training, tool execution or reproduction was performed.

## Live-SWE-agent: Can Software Engineering Agents Self-Evolve on the Fly?

**2025-11-17 · preprint · adjacent · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.13646)

**Mechanism.** Adds tool-creation instructions and step-level reminders to a bash-based mini-SWE-agent loop. The agent writes, revises and executes Python helper scripts during one issue. The evaluated loop and model weights remain fixed; saving tools across independent tasks is proposed future work.

**What changes:** Tools. **Persistence:** within-task. **Learning signal:** Current-issue execution feedback and repeated prompts to consider useful tool creation guide the agent.

**Evaluation.** ArXiv v3 reports one patch per issue on 500 SWE-bench Verified and 731 SWE-Bench Pro tasks, with 250-step and three-dollar caps. It includes a 50-task component/model ablation, a 50-task multilingual test and imported comparisons with offline-evolved agents.

**Boundary.** This is within-task tool synthesis, not demonstrated persistent cross-task learning. On the ablation subset GPT-5-Nano drops from 44% to 14%, and GPT-5-Mini also declines slightly. Baselines include imported results; repeated-run uncertainty is absent. Historical rankings and costs are not current guarantees.

## Self-Harmony: Learning to Harmonize Self-Supervision and Self-Play in Test-Time Reinforcement Learning

**2025-11-03 · peer-reviewed · ICLR 2026 · adjacent · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.01191)

**Mechanism.** A shared model generates original-solution and fused reframe-and-solve trajectories. Harmonic aggregation of their answer frequencies selects pseudo-labels for reinforcement learning. A separate model is adapted for each benchmark; agreement supplies a learning signal, not an independent correctness check.

**What changes:** Model weights. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Agreement among model answers to original and reframed questions supplies pseudo-labels, with format/diversity reward terms.

**Evaluation.** Full v2 review covers five models and six benchmarks, 16-rollout mean pass@1, component and reward ablations, inference-only voting, semantic-shift analyses and complete theoretical appendices. Main results are transductive: adaptation and scoring use the same unlabeled questions.

**Boundary.** Reframing can change meaning; external-model answer agreement is an imperfect semantic check. Rollout-count matching does not match total compute, and some baselines use peak rather than final scores. No independent training-run uncertainty is reported. Curator analysis identifies a rank-equivalence gap in the Infomax derivation; empirical gains should not be presented as a correctness guarantee.

## OpenSIR: Open-Ended Self-Improving Reasoner

**2025-11-01 · preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.00602)

**Mechanism.** Updates one policy in teacher and student roles with GRPO-style training, expanding a problem pool from a trivial seed. Novelty selects generation and solving examples; a separate seven-billion-parameter embedding model supplies the diversity signal.

**What changes:** Model weights. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Majority-answer agreement supplies student pseudo-labels; solve rate, solution length and pretrained-encoder distance reward generated problems.

**Evaluation.** ArXiv v4 studies four post-trained models, seven math and three general-reasoning benchmarks over three training seeds. It reports Pass@1 averaged over sixteen samples per question, component/seed ablations, human problem reviews and a longer single-run study.

**Boundary.** Consensus is not ground truth; human problem validity and GPT-5 answer agreement are distinct measures. Student training pairs are matched, but total rollout batches double. Embedding dispersion is not proof of new mathematical knowledge, and the extended run plateaus after roughly 300 steps.

## SPICE: Self-Play In Corpus Environments Improves Reasoning

**2025-10-28 · preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.24684)

**Mechanism.** One shared model learns challenger and reasoner roles through role-centered policy updates. The challenger sees a sampled document; the reasoner receives its generated question. Weights change within a fixed training and task-generation framework.

**What changes:** Model weights. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** The challenger produces document-conditioned questions and answer labels. Math-Verify or exact matching scores agreement with those labels; a Gaussian reward favors intermediate solver success rates. Formatting validity is checked separately from factual correctness.

**Evaluation.** Four Qwen/OctoThinker models are evaluated on seven math and four general-reasoning benchmarks after training on 20,000 documents. Controls vary corpus, format, challenger training and reward; AIME uses average accuracy over 32 samples.

**Boundary.** Document access and answer matching do not independently certify generated questions or labels. Baselines differ in rollout budgets. Some appendix averages disagree with their listed scores, qualifying claims that mixed corpora/formats are always best. A fixed corpus and training horizon do not establish sustained open-ended learning.

## Search Self-Play: Pushing the Frontier of Agent Capability without Supervision

**2025-10-21 · peer-reviewed · ICLR 2026 · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.18821)

**Mechanism.** Trains one model in proposer and solver roles using REINFORCE and GRPO. Search-grounded questions pass format rules and RAG verification with distractor documents. The main implementation reuses valid questions and clears its replay buffer every ten updates; learned behavior persists in weights.

**What changes:** Model weights. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** A fixed Qwen2.5-32B verifier and judge assess generated questions and solver answers against supplied seed answers. Solver failure rewards the proposer; valid questions are reused in a periodically cleared buffer.

**Evaluation.** Full v3 and Appendices A–E cover seven sampled QA benchmarks, several model families/sizes, continued training of search checkpoints, filtering and replay controls, algorithm/runtime trade-offs, and a failed negative-reward configuration. Outcomes are model-judged pass@1.

**Boundary.** 50,000 seed answers come from public training sets, and a stronger model supplies verification and judgment. Each benchmark uses 500 questions except Bamboogle’s 125, with fixed Wikipedia retrieval and ten search calls. RAG agreement cannot ensure unique valid questions. Reported gains lack independent training-seed uncertainty; rollout-time comparisons are not total-cost matches.

## MARSHAL: Incentivizing Multi-Agent Reasoning via Self-Play with Strategic LLMs

**2025-10-17 · peer-reviewed · ICLR 2026 · core · paper**

**Mechanism.** Updates a shared language model through cooperative and competitive self-play in fixed games. Turn-level returns are mean-centered within player-role groups. Learned weights transfer into fixed debate or cooperation workflows; the workflows themselves do not evolve.

**What changes:** Model weights. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Game outcomes plus engineered action-format and response-length rewards guide online reinforcement learning.

**Evaluation.** Full arXiv v3 review covers three training games, three held-out games, seven reasoning benchmarks in single-agent/MAD/AutoGen settings, 4B/8B models, raw returns and all appendix controls. Authors report higher average downstream scores, alongside task-specific regressions.

Independent training-run uncertainty and matched generalist/specialist compute are not established. As printed, several MAD appendix ablations outperform full specialists, so component necessity is not uniform. Qualitative traces do not establish causal theory-of-mind gains.

**2025-09-29 · peer-reviewed · ICLR 2026 · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.25140)

**Mechanism.** Extracts short strategy notes from successes and failures, appends them to persistent memory, and retrieves notes from similar prior queries. Parallel or sequential memory-aware test-time scaling supplies additional experiences; model weights and the memory-update procedure remain fixed.

**What changes:** Memory. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** The agent’s backbone judges completed trajectories without reference answers in the main task stream. Multiple attempts provide contrastive evidence; a separate diagnostic injects label noise using ground truth.

**Boundary.** Fewer interaction steps do not imply fewer total tokens: the reported cost breakdown includes a modest token increase over no memory. Simulated independent label flips do not capture every correlated judge error. Task-order sensitivity, long-term forgetting and repeated-run uncertainty are not established; strategy emergence is illustrated qualitatively.

**2025-09-29 · peer-reviewed · ICML 2026 · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.02373)

**Mechanism.** Wraps a fixed agent with structured-path generation, consensus/safety validation and a separate lesson store. Query- and action-related retrieval brings previous failure patterns into pre-execution review. The main implementation uses model judgments rather than a pure majority vote.

**What changes:** Memory. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** An LLM judges query-grounded reasoning paths for consistency and unsafe intent; flagged paths become negative lessons consulted in later action checks.

**Evaluation.** The final ICML paper tests direct poisoning on StrategyQA/EHRAgent, indirect injection on MMLU, collaborative misinformation and adaptive attacks, including malicious-majority retrieval. ASR-t is one minus exact-match accuracy and includes ordinary model errors; benign accuracy also falls in some settings. Adaptive tests are bounded, and structural visualizations do not certify safety. More retrieved lessons can hurt utility; long-term protection and deployment cost remain uncertain.

**Mechanism.** Provides a synthetic, chronological campus environment with persistent calendars, bookings and other state, while raw model context resets between tasks. StuGPA combines exam, class and daily-life outcomes; retention and initiative metrics test tool-mediated information use and scheduled action.

## Memento: Fine-tuning LLM Agents without Fine-tuning LLMs

**2025-08-22 · preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.16153)

**Mechanism.** A planner–executor agent retains final-state, plan and outcome cases. Retrieval uses fixed embedding similarity or a trained Q-network with top-k selection; this implementation simplifies the general multi-step soft-Q formulation to single-step prediction.

**What changes:** Memory, Model weights. **Persistence:** both. **Learning signal:** Task outcomes label stored plans. The implemented parametric variant trains a separate retrieval network with binary cross-entropy on success feedback; the underlying LLMs remain frozen.

**Evaluation.** GAIA validation uses three passes with accumulating memory; test evaluation uses the validation-built bank. Separate QA transfer builds memory on four datasets before testing three others. Memory, planning, retrieval-size and model-choice ablations are reported.

**Boundary.** Repeated-task gains do not establish open-ended learning, and the no-memory baseline also improves across iterations. The stated weighted QA average conflicts with displayed values; model-judged partial-match scores are not established as equivalent to official leaderboards. Cross-system models and compute differ; uncertainty and lifecycle costs remain incomplete.

**Code / data.** [Official artifact](https://github.com/Memento-Teams/Memento) — Author-linked repository README at commit 42fbbcac63dd58ed6856c0761357345a58e4f032 inspected on 2026-11-09. It documents both retrieval variants and separate retriever training; not executed.

**Topics:** memory, continual-learning, applications. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-11-09.

## A Comprehensive Survey of Self-Evolving AI Agents: A New Paradigm Bridging Foundation Models and Lifelong Agentic Systems

**2025-08-10 · preprint · core · survey**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.07407)

**Mechanism.** Connects system inputs, an agent system, environment feedback and an optimizer over a defined search space. It separates task-level from instance-level optimization and surveys model behavior, prompts, memory, tools, multi-agent topology and domain-specific workflows.

**What changes:** Analysis / no retained update. **Persistence:** not-applicable. **Learning signal:** Not applicable to the survey itself; its organizing loop compares task metrics, execution feedback, demonstrations and model-generated evaluations used by agent optimizers.

**Evaluation.** ArXiv v2 synthesizes methods through August 2025 and discusses tool, web, software, scientific and multimodal benchmarks alongside model/agent judges. It proposes safety-first, performance-preserving evolution principles and identifies longitudinal evaluation, transfer, reward quality and cost as open problems.

**Boundary.** The broad optimization umbrella includes transient inference search and externally trained systems, not only persistent autonomous learning. Its three laws are design aspirations, not demonstrated guarantees. No reproducible screening funnel or pooled comparison is provided, and at least one cited method is misdescribed; primary-paper checks remain necessary.

**Code / data.** [Official artifact](https://github.com/EvoAgentX/Awesome-Self-Evolving-Agents) — Author-linked survey collection introduction and taxonomy inspected on 2026-11-09. This is a literature resource; its listings were not individually reproduced or treated as primary evidence for other papers.

**Topics:** surveys, architecture, continual-learning. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-11-09.

<a id="temporal-self-rewarding"></a>

## Temporal Self-Rewarding Language Models: Decoupling Chosen-Rejected via Past-Future

**2025-08-08 · peer-reviewed · ICML 2026 · adjacent · paper**

[Primary source](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v306/wang26ik.html)

**Mechanism.** Selects rejected answers from the lower-scoring initial/current candidates, trains a temporary model, then chooses better-scoring current/temporary answers. A second DPO stage starts again from the current model using these new pairs. Updated weights persist; the judge, candidate sources and selection rules define the learning signal.

**What changes:** Model weights. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Current-model preference scores rank outputs from initial, current and temporary trained models. Initialization uses external instruction/evaluation data and GPT-4o explanations; the separate online math extension uses correctness-filtered reference solutions.

**Evaluation.** The ICML 2026 paper compares five backbone/size configurations on three instruction benchmarks, four downstream tasks and a separate GRPO math extension. Two temporal iterations are compared with four standard self-rewarding iterations, alongside past/future and external-judge ablations.

**Boundary.** Matching DPO stage counts does not establish equal generation, judging or total compute. GPT-4o judging and response length affect the reported win rates; gains vary by metric and iteration. Conditional gradient analysis does not prove indefinite stable learning. Some tables and the current artifact pair rules disagree with the paper.

**Code / data.** [Official artifact](https://github.com/TemporalSelfRewarding/TSR) — Official README inspected on 2026-11-09. It documents later corrections and pair-selection options that differ from paper pseudocode; its archived reproduction claims were not independently checked here. No research code, datasets, training or evaluation executed.

**Topics:** model-training, self-play, evaluation. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-11-09.

<a id="memp"></a>

## Memp: Exploring Agent Procedural Memory

**2025-08-08 · peer-reviewed · Findings of ACL 2026 · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.06433)

**Mechanism.** Combines detailed trajectories with abstract procedural scripts in an external memory bank. Similarity retrieval supplies guidance to fixed-weight agents; online variants append experience, keep successes or revise a retrieved procedure after failure.

**What changes:** Memory, Skills. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Successful training trajectories initialize memory; benchmark success feedback selects, revises or filters later experience.

**Evaluation.** The Findings of ACL paper evaluates TravelPlanner and ALFWorld with three models, comparing memory formats, retrieval keys and sequential update policies. It also transfers GPT-4o memories to Qwen2.5-14B and varies retrieval count.

**Boundary.** ALFWorld gains do not imply uniformly better planning: GPT-4o and Claude hard-constraint scores on TravelPlanner fall below no-memory baselines. Online updates rely on benchmark rewards; exact task counts, ordering and uncertainty are insufficiently specified in the paper. Cross-model reuse is not unrelated-domain transfer.

**Code / data.** [Official artifact](https://github.com/zjunlp/MemP) — Official repository linked and its public page inspected; not executed.

**Topics:** memory, skills, continual-learning. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-11-09.

<a id="r-zero"></a>

## R-Zero: Self-Evolving Reasoning LLM from Zero Data

**2025-08-07 · peer-reviewed · ICLR 2026 · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.05004)

**Mechanism.** Alternates GRPO updates of separate challenger and solver copies. The challenger proposes mostly mathematical questions; the solver samples answers, filters questions by agreement and trains toward its own majority answer. Updated model weights persist between rounds, with fixed human-designed prompts and reward rules.

**What changes:** Model weights. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Solver majority votes provide pseudo-labels; disagreement, formatting and repetition signals reward the challenger. No independent correctness oracle supervises the main training loop.

**Evaluation.** ArXiv v4 evaluates four backbones on seven mathematical and three general-reasoning benchmarks after three rounds, with additional iteration, shared-parameter, curriculum, supervised-data and pseudo-label diagnostics. Some contest results use mean accuracy over 32 samples; others use greedy decoding.

**Boundary.** Agreement is not correctness. Longer training eventually degrades and external-model diagnostics find worsening pseudo-label accuracy. Gains vary across tasks and several table/prose values conflict. The theoretical reward motivation does not guarantee a correct curriculum or indefinite improvement; pretrained knowledge and designed prompts remain inputs.

**Code / data.** [Official artifact](https://github.com/Chengsong-Huang/R-Zero) — Official paper-linked README and training/release descriptions inspected on 2026-11-09; no models, datasets or research code run. Later R-Few work and older README scores are not substituted for the reviewed R-Zero v4 results.

**Topics:** model-training, self-play. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-11-09.

## A Survey of Self-Evolving Agents: What, When, How, and Where to Evolve on the Path to Artificial Super Intelligence

**2025-07-28 · peer-reviewed · TMLR 2026 · core · survey**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.21046)

**Mechanism.** Organizes agent changes by what evolves, when updates occur, how feedback drives them and where they are applied. A trajectory-conditioned system update formalism separates model, context, tools and architecture, while the survey includes both early feedback-driven mechanisms and stronger autonomous reconfiguration.

**What changes:** Analysis / no retained update. **Persistence:** not-applicable. **Learning signal:** Not applicable to the survey itself; it distinguishes feedback type/source, demonstrations, population fitness, timing and update targets across surveyed systems.

**Evaluation.** ArXiv v4, matching the January 2026 TMLR title, synthesizes methods and proposes five evaluation goals: adaptivity, retention, generalization, efficiency and safety. It details short/long-horizon protocols, forgetting and backward-transfer probes, cost accounting, human intervention and benchmark coverage gaps.

**Boundary.** Survey inclusion does not prove persistent learning or recursive improvement. Protocols and gap claims are a historical synthesis, not a pooled experiment or certification. Some mechanism labels and numerical examples conflict with primary evidence or arithmetic; cost-per-gain also needs explicit treatment of zero or negative gains.

## GEPA: Reflective Prompt Evolution Can Outperform Reinforcement Learning

**2025-07-25 · peer-reviewed · ICLR 2026 · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.19457)

**Mechanism.** Mutates module instructions using trace reflection, retains complementary candidates through instance-wise Pareto selection, and optionally merges prompt sets from separate lineages. The executor weights and control flow stay fixed. A separate inference-time variant searches solutions on the target tasks themselves.

**What changes:** Prompts / context. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Training execution/evaluation traces and per-module feedback generate mutations; validation scores select candidates.

**Evaluation.** ArXiv v2 compares six tasks on Qwen3-8B and GPT-4.1 Mini, including GRPO, prompt optimizers, selection ablations and cross-model transfer. It also reports kernel search and an adversarial instruction-following probe.

**Boundary.** Rollout budgets include validation but omit separate reflection calls; they are not total compute. GRPO is stronger on Qwen AIME; merging hurts several Qwen tasks. Main results lack independent search-run uncertainty. Kernel search is not held-out transfer, and the adversarial accuracy collapse largely reflects answer-format failure.

**2025-07-04 · preprint · core · paper**

**Mechanism.** A shared policy plays both roles in fixed language games and learns from terminal outcomes. Separate moving-average baselines for each game and role reduce update variance. Model weights evolve while game rules, rewards and the training procedure remain fixed.

## Self-Adapting Language Models

**2025-06-12 · peer-reviewed · NeurIPS 2025 · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.10943)

**Mechanism.** An outer filtered-training loop learns to generate useful self-edits, while an inner gradient update adapts model weights. Knowledge edits generate training text; ARC edits select predefined augmentations and tuning settings. The update framework itself stays fixed.

**What changes:** Model weights. **Persistence:** both. **Learning signal:** Training-time downstream performance after actual adaptation selects self-edits. ARC uses supplied target grids; knowledge evaluation uses reference answers and GPT-4.1 grading. External inputs, evaluation tasks and adaptation tools remain supplied.

**Evaluation.** ArXiv v2 studies no-context SQuAD knowledge incorporation, joint continued pretraining, and 40 sampled adaptation configurations on eight preselected ARC evaluation tasks. Appendices add prompting, alternative-generator and proxy-reward comparisons; sequential edits test forgetting.

**Boundary.** ARC results are conditional on preselected solvable tasks. Stronger prompt baselines exceed the default learned-edit result, although training also improves those prompts. Some competing generators win in other settings. Sequential edits still forget; labeled evaluation and expensive candidate fine-tuning constrain broader continual learning.

**2025-06-09 · peer-reviewed · NeurIPS 2025 · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.07398)

**Mechanism.** Maintains linked insight, query and interaction graphs with fixed models and orchestration. Similar-query retrieval, graph traversal, trajectory compression and role-specific projection supply memories at task onset; completed tasks update the hierarchy.

**What changes:** Memory. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Completed multi-agent trajectories, task-resolution feedback and resource statistics drive memory updates; some configured agents have access to reference-based evaluation.

<a id="self-challenging-agents"></a>

## Self-Challenging Language Model Agents

**2025-06-02 · peer-reviewed · NeurIPS 2025 · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.01716)

**Mechanism.** A fixed challenger explores tools and proposes Code-as-Task instructions and checks. In the main self-improvement setting, successful offline trajectories from the same 8B model are used for rejection fine-tuning of the executor; a separate setting distills 70B demonstrations. The challenger itself is not iteratively trained in these experiments.

**What changes:** Model weights. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Generated executable checks provide binary rewards; passing examples and failure cases filter candidate tasks. Tool environments, prompt examples and verification scaffolding are supplied externally.

**Evaluation.** ArXiv v1 compares four environments from M3ToolEval and modified Tau-Bench, with four evaluation trials. It reports 12.0% to 23.5% average pass@1 for self-training and 32.2% with teacher distillation, plus verifier ablations, task/trajectory scaling, online-RL diagnostics and joint-training comparisons.

**Boundary.** Generated tests do not guarantee semantic correctness: filtering retains about 5% of Retail candidates and false negatives remain. Airline excludes no-action-success tasks, browsing is synthetic and improvements are mainly environment-specific. Prompt examples and baseline judging choices matter; online RL can collapse and annotation sample counts are inconsistent.

**Code / data.** Official runnable code was not verified in this source review.

**Topics:** model-training, self-play, tools. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-11-09.

**2025-05-29 · peer-reviewed · ICLR 2026 · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.22954)

**Mechanism.** Selected coding agents modify their own implementation, and an archive retains functional variants, including weaker candidates that may support later improvements. Agent tools and workflows evolve; foundation models, diagnostic prompting, archive management and parent selection remain fixed.

**What changes:** Agent code, Tools, Workflows, Prompts / context. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Coding-benchmark outcomes and logs inform a separate fixed o1 diagnostic model, which proposes changes for the selected coding agent to implement. The SWE-bench diagnosis prompt includes private-test information from prior evaluations.

**Boundary.** The 50% SWE-bench result is on a 200-task subset used during search. Staged selection, private-test diagnostic feedback and higher compute than baselines qualify the main curves; cross-benchmark tests provide stronger transfer evidence. A perfect hallucination score was obtained by bypassing logging-based detection, not by solving hallucination.

## LifelongAgentBench: Evaluating LLM Agents as Lifelong Learners

**2025-05-17 · preprint · core · benchmark**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.11942)

**Mechanism.** Sequences tasks with overlapping SQL, shell-command and knowledge-graph skills and retains interaction histories for fixed-weight agents. Database tables and operating-system containers reset between tasks. Group self-consistency splits replay into multiple inference contexts and votes on the next action.

**What changes:** Memory, Skills. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Environment-verified task outcomes determine which recent successful trajectories enter replay; group variants vote over actions conditioned on separate experience subsets.

**Evaluation.** ArXiv v3 contains 500 database, 500 operating-system and 396 knowledge-graph tasks. It varies replay size, model backbone, task difficulty and grouping, reporting task success and average input length alongside format, context and execution-failure examples.

**Boundary.** Replay can hurt stronger baselines or exhaust memory. Grouping shortens each context but adds inference calls, so it does not establish equal-compute efficiency. Shared skills do not imply persistent environment state, and the results do not directly measure forgetting over revisited old tasks. Some appendix error explanations are incorrect.

## Absolute Zero: Reinforced Self-play Reasoning with Zero Data

**2025-05-06 · peer-reviewed · NeurIPS 2025 · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.03335)

**Mechanism.** A shared pretrained model proposes and solves three kinds of code-reasoning tasks. Joint reinforcement learning updates both roles, and a buffer retains valid generated tasks for subsequent proposals and training. Task formats, verification and the optimization procedure remain fixed.

**What changes:** Model weights. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Python execution checks sampled task/answer agreement. The proposer reward depends on eight sampled solver attempts, favoring difficult but sometimes solvable tasks; it is a proxy for learnability, not measured future improvement.

**Evaluation.** ArXiv v3 compares coding and mathematics benchmarks across model families and sizes, with task/proposer ablations, high-pass@k coverage and MMLU-Pro results. Appendices report unsuccessful curriculum, reward and preprocessing alternatives.

**Boundary.** Zero data concerns new curated post-training tasks, not pretraining or human-designed rules. Finite execution checks do not prove program equivalence or faithful reasoning; retained globals can leak answers. Some benchmarks regress, and model/data budgets differ across baselines. Bounded results do not establish unlimited or safe autonomous improvement.

## Mem0: Building Production-Ready AI Agents with Scalable Long-Term Memory

**2025-04-28 · preprint · adjacent · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.19413)

**Mechanism.** Extracts facts from recent exchanges and background summaries, then updates an external memory store through add/update/delete/no-op decisions. The graph variant stores entities and relations and can invalidate obsolete edges; neither variant trains model weights during memory management.

**What changes:** Memory. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Conversation messages, summaries and LLM decisions about whether candidate facts add, update, contradict or duplicate stored information.

**Evaluation.** LoCoMo conversational QA excluding adversarial questions, with lexical metrics, repeated judge scoring and query-time latency/token measurements. The full-context baseline has higher overall judge accuracy; graph memory helps some categories but trails base Mem0 on single- and multi-hop questions.

**Boundary.** Query-time savings do not include the full cost of building and updating memory. Hosted/manual baselines and imported results require version-matched protocols; A-MEM category labels differ across the compared documents. The permissive judge and exclusion of unanswerable questions limit factuality/abstention conclusions. Production readiness is not independently established.

**Code / data.** Code availability not verified in this review.

**Topics:** memory, evaluation. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-11-09.

<a id="ragen"></a>

## RAGEN: Understanding Self-Evolution in LLM Agents via Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning

**2025-04-24 · preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.20073)

**Mechanism.** StarPO organizes trajectory collection and PPO/GRPO updates to model weights. StarPO-S tests variability-based prompt filtering and gradient changes, including KL removal and asymmetric clipping. These are externally specified training interventions, not agent-written changes to the learning algorithm.

**What changes:** Model weights. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Task rewards on multi-turn trajectories drive policy updates. Within-prompt reward variability is used for filtering; entropy and gradient statistics diagnose training behavior.

**Evaluation.** ArXiv v2 studies Bandit, Sokoban, FrozenLake and WebShop, with model-size, rollout-frequency, action-budget and distribution-shift analyses. It reports collapse and spurious reasoning, plus an appendix comparison where supervised learning from search-generated trajectories outperforms RL on Sokoban.

**Boundary.** Stochastic reward variance is not calibrated knowledge uncertainty, and shorter reasoning text does not alone prove loss of reasoning ability. Stabilization benefits vary by task and optimizer. Small environments, limited repeat-run reporting and inconsistent horizon descriptions constrain generalization. The current RAGEN-2 software and paper are distinct from this study.

**Code / data.** [Official artifact](https://github.com/mll-lab-nu/RAGEN) — Official current README inspected on 2026-11-09; it distinguishes original RAGEN from later RAGEN-2 and related releases. No installation, training, model or environment execution; the current branch is not treated as a reproduction of arXiv v2.

**Topics:** model-training, evaluation, applications. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-11-09.

## A Self-Improving Coding Agent

**2025-04-21 · preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.15228)

**Mechanism.** Selects the best prior agent from an archive to modify its own Python implementation, then evaluates the resulting agent. Tools, prompts and orchestration can persist into later modification attempts, while the outer archive-selection and evaluation loop stays fixed.

**What changes:** Agent code, Tools, Workflows. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** A fixed utility combines benchmark scores, dollar cost and elapsed time. Archived results and traces guide subsequent code modifications; no model-weight training is performed.

**Evaluation.** ArXiv v2 reports a fifteen-iteration coding run on reused SWE-bench Verified and LiveCodeBench subsets plus synthetic editing/navigation tasks. A separate AIME/GPQA run finds little improvement. Per-iteration scores, costs and times reveal regressions as well as gains.

**Boundary.** No independently held-out final task set or fixed-modifier ablation is reported. Short timeouts make editing efficiency a major contributor; best-so-far utility is not monotonic task improvement. Paper and current-code subset settings differ, and broader run variance remains unclear. Observability is not a demonstrated safety guarantee.

**Code / data.** [Official artifact](https://github.com/MaximeRobeyns/self_improving_coding_agent) — Official README and selected benchmark code at ed8275dca4d3c5dbf77229964351fe9b424797dc inspected on 2026-11-09. The current SWE scorer uses binary harness resolution, but its default subset differs from the paper. No code, containers or benchmarks were executed.

**Topics:** architecture, recursive-improvement, applications. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-11-09.

**2025-02-17 · peer-reviewed · NeurIPS 2025 · core · paper**

**Mechanism.** Creates atomic notes, retrieves candidate neighbors by embedding similarity, links relevant notes, and revises neighboring contextual attributes. Persistent external notes change subsequent retrieval; model weights remain fixed.

**What changes:** Memory. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** New conversation content and LLM-generated contextual descriptions, tags, relationship decisions and neighbor updates.

**Evaluation.** LoCoMo and DialSim conversational QA; six main-table models plus three appendix models, link/evolution ablations, retrieval-size sweeps and storage/retrieval scaling. Category-level comparisons require resolving the version-specific table-label differences described below.

Table 1 in v5 and v11 assigns different category names to unchanged score columns, and v11 retains a twofold multi-hop claim inconsistent with its displayed labels. Category-specific gains remain uncertain until the labeling is reconciled.

## Agent-R: Training Language Model Agents to Reflect via Iterative Self-Training

**2025-01-20 · preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.11425)

**Mechanism.** Builds synthetic recovery trajectories by truncating a bad branch and appending a good continuation. Iterative supervised training updates the actor on good and revised trajectories, with loss focused on the revision and continuation. The search, selection and training procedure itself stays fixed.

**What changes:** Model weights. **Persistence:** both. **Learning signal:** Environment terminal rewards select contrasting tree-search paths; the current actor identifies a revision point. Training also includes ShareGPT data and manually written revision connectors.

**Evaluation.** Three Llama-3.1-8B training rounds evaluate WebShop/ScienceWorld reward and TextCraft success. Separate tests continue truncated failures from the original model, and analyses examine repeated actions, revision positions and multi-task training.

**Boundary.** Earlier self-identified errors are not independently measured localization accuracy. Spliced trajectories assume compatible environment states; the inspected construction code assembles logs without replaying the combined path at that stage. Metrics, baseline training and data budgets differ; repeated-run uncertainty and generalization beyond the three environments remain unestablished.

**Code / data.** [Official artifact](https://github.com/ByteDance-Seed/Agent-R) — Paper-linked repository redirects to ByteDance-Seed/Agent-R. README and trajectory-construction code at 82fcc1ca7873b460949ed49022146dd988c32e31 inspected on 2026-11-09; no code, environments or training were executed, and paper-result reproduction is not established.

**Topics:** model-training, foundations, applications. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-11-09.

## LongMemEval: Benchmarking Chat Assistants on Long-Term Interactive Memory

**2024-10-14 · peer-reviewed · ICLR 2025 · adjacent · benchmark**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.10813)

**Mechanism.** Constructs 500 curated questions with annotated evidence embedded in scalable user-assistant histories, testing extraction, multi-session reasoning, updates, temporal reasoning and abstention. It separates indexing, retrieval and reading, then varies their designs without training a continually improving policy.

**What changes:** Memory. **Persistence:** not-applicable. **Learning signal:** Not applicable: analysis or evaluation resource.

**Evaluation.** Studies roughly 115k-token and 1.5M-token histories, retrieval granularity, fact-expanded keys, temporal filters and reader prompts. A GPT-4o judge is checked against humans on thirty responses per question type from each of two answer models; retrieval and answer scores are reported separately.

**Boundary.** Histories combine simulated/human-edited evidence with sampled background sessions. The 97-question commercial-system study used shorter histories in August 2024 and omitted several abilities. Reader and query-model choices affect gains; retrieval correctness can require obsolete evidence unnecessary for a correct updated answer. Recall scores do not establish procedural learning.

**Code / data.** [Official artifact](https://github.com/xiaowu0162/LongMemEval) — Official repository linked and inspected; not installed or executed.

**Topics:** evaluation, memory. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-11-09.

## AFlow: Automating Agentic Workflow Generation

**2024-10-14 · peer-reviewed · ICLR 2025 · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.10762)

**Mechanism.** Searches Python workflow structure and custom prompts with an MCTS-inspired selection/expansion loop. Actual experiments fix models, temperatures and output formats and provide reusable operators. Selected workflows and tree-organized experience persist; the optimizer itself is unchanged.

**What changes:** Workflows, Prompts / context, Agent code. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Validation-set scores and execution logs, including expected answers, guide a fixed LLM optimizer. Code workflows can also use supplied public tests and generated tests during solution refinement.

**Evaluation.** Six reasoning/QA/code benchmarks use a seeded validation/test split, five validation evaluations per candidate and three test evaluations. Studies include cross-model workflow transfer, a GSM8K operator ablation, inference-cost comparisons and small judged writing/idea-generation cases.

**Boundary.** Repeated executions do not measure independent search-run variance. Gains mix task metrics, and inference-cost comparisons exclude search costs. Algorithm descriptions differ in selection details; the theoretical discussion does not prove finite global optimality. Open-ended cases remain small and do not independently establish novelty or exact constraint satisfaction.

**Code / data.** [Official artifact](https://github.com/FoundationAgents/AFlow) — Official README inspected on 2026-11-09; it documents APIs, operators and evaluation resources, and notes possible operator issues after migration from MetaGPT. No research code, datasets or benchmark runs were executed.

## AgentSquare: Automatic LLM Agent Search in Modular Design Space

**2024-10-08 · peer-reviewed · ICLR 2025 · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.06153)

**Mechanism.** Alternates code-level module evolution with recombination of planning, reasoning, tool-use and memory modules. Novel modules receive environment evaluation; recombinations use an LLM surrogate. Module pools and scored designs persist within a fixed external search procedure.

**What changes:** Workflows, Prompts / context, Tools, Memory. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Task-performance evaluations and an in-context predictor conditioned on examples of previously evaluated module combinations.

**Evaluation.** GPT-3.5 and GPT-4o comparisons on WebShop, ALFWorld, ScienceWorld, M3ToolEval, TravelPlanner and PDDL, with module ablations, surrogate-versus-observed plots and search/execution-cost analyses. Reported metrics differ across tasks: success, reward, progress and micro pass rate.

**Boundary.** Search remains constrained by standardized interfaces. Execution-cost plots exclude search costs, which are tabulated separately. The inspected paper does not specify a separate held-out search/test partition or independent-run uncertainty; surrogate correlation is not a guarantee that novel designs generalize.

## Gödel Agent: A Self-Referential Agent Framework for Recursive Self-Improvement

**2024-10-06 · peer-reviewed · ACL 2025 (proceedings title uses Recursively Self-Improvement) · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.04444)

**Mechanism.** Uses runtime code inspection and monkey patching to revise both task-solving functions and parts of the improvement process. Human-specified goals, interfaces and initial tools provide the starting conditions; the experiments do not train the underlying model weights.

**What changes:** Agent code, Prompts / context, Workflows. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Validation-task scores and error information guide changes to the solver and its self-modification logic.

**Evaluation.** The ACL paper searches six times per task, up to thirty iterations, with a GPT-4o optimizer on DROP, MGSM, MMLU and GPQA. The constrained executor uses GPT-3.5; unrestricted results can invoke stronger models. Game-of-24 and robustness studies provide further diagnostics.

**Boundary.** Baselines are imported from prior work, and test-bootstrap intervals do not measure search-run variation. In 100 MGSM trials, 14% finish worse and 4% terminate unexpectedly. Unrestricted scores and historical cost estimates are not controlled equal-resource comparisons or proofs of unlimited improvement.

## Training Language Models to Self-Correct via Reinforcement Learning

**2024-09-19 · peer-reviewed · ICLR 2025 · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.12917)

**Mechanism.** Trains one model through two-turn online RL: first constrain initial answers while learning revisions, then optimize both turns with a progress bonus. The learned weights persist across problems; each test-time revision remains a within-problem operation.

**What changes:** Model weights. **Persistence:** both. **Learning signal:** Ground-truth answer checks and unit tests reward self-generated training traces; no correctness oracle is supplied for test-time revision.

**Evaluation.** ArXiv v2 evaluates Gemini models on MATH500 and HumanEval after MATH/MBPP training, with offline MBPP-R repair, component ablations and repeated-attempt tests. MATH training incorporates 4,500 original test problems while reserving 500 for evaluation.

**Boundary.** The 15.6-point MATH headline is improvement in the correction delta, not final-answer accuracy. Training uses oracle rewards and training-reward checkpoint selection; code first-attempt accuracy can decline. Only two attempts are trained, and answer-level reward does not verify every reasoning step.

**Code / data.** Official runnable code was not verified in this source review.

**Topics:** model-training, foundations. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-11-09.

## Agent Workflow Memory

**2024-09-11 · peer-reviewed · ICML 2025 · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.07429)

**Mechanism.** Abstracts reusable subtask workflows and inserts them into agent context. Offline workflows are induced before evaluation; online workflows accumulate after completed tasks. Experiments group tasks and workflow stores by website. Executable workflow shortcuts are a separate variant.

**What changes:** Memory, Workflows. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Annotated offline demonstrations or completed online trajectories accepted by a model-based success evaluator; model weights stay fixed.

**Evaluation.** The final ICML paper evaluates WebArena, a cross-template subset and Mind2Web, with representation, mixed-memory, task-order and cost analyses. Its Mind2Web headline improvement is in step success, distinct from whole-task completion.

**Boundary.** Combining offline and online memories can hurt; executable shortcuts improve step scores while reducing whole-task success in the displayed table. Task-order evidence covers small website groups. Model identifiers and some baseline rows conflict across the final paper, limiting exact comparison claims. Learned success judgments can admit faulty workflows.

## Automated Design of Agentic Systems

**2024-08-15 · peer-reviewed · ICLR 2025 · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.08435)

**Mechanism.** A fixed meta-agent writes executable forward functions, checks novelty, repairs execution errors, and archives designs with scores. Search changes prompts and control flow in task agents; the outer search algorithm and model weights are fixed.

**What changes:** Agent code, Workflows, Prompts / context. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Validation-task scores, runtime errors and an archive of earlier code designs; the pretrained meta-agent proposes and reflects on candidates.

**Evaluation.** ARC grid-transformation code and DROP, MGSM, MMLU and GPQA; cross-domain/model transfer and empty-archive controls. ARC uses 20 validation and 60 test problems with grids at most 5 by 5; reported intervals are bootstrap estimates, not independent search-run variation.

**Boundary.** Experiments concern bounded question-answering tasks; continual deployment and optimization of the meta-agent are proposed future work. ## Recursive Introspection: Teaching Language Model Agents How to Self-Improve

**2024-07-25 · peer-reviewed · NeurIPS 2024 · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.18219)

**Mechanism.** Converts a problem into a sequence of attempted answers and trains a correction policy with reward-weighted learning on accumulated rollouts. At deployment, fixed-weight revisions concern the current problem: oracle stopping or checker-free majority voting are alternative protocols.

**What changes:** Model weights. **Persistence:** both. **Learning signal:** Training uses reference-answer checks to select better responses from the learner or a stronger teacher. The main teacher-assisted setup includes a knowledge-boosting stage; the self-distillation experiment is separate.

**Evaluation.** The final NeurIPS paper includes math comparisons, up to ten-turn evaluation, cross-dataset and model-transfer analyses, and added MBPP/CoNaLa results. Controls compare sequential and parallel sampling, training-data composition and preservation of correct answers.

**Boundary.** Equal sample counts do not guarantee equal token or latency budgets. The single-iteration self-distillation variant trails parallel sampling from the same trained model. Some first-turn scores regress; the checklist reports no repeated training runs. Code-task protocols are less detailed than math experiments, and bounded correction is not recursive improvement of the training algorithm.

## Symbolic Learning Enables Self-Evolving Agents

**2024-06-26 · preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.18532)

**Mechanism.** Records an execution trajectory, propagates natural-language critiques backward, and edits prompts, tool definitions and pipeline configuration with fixed LLMs. Invalid edits are retried; a rollback check reevaluates the current training example. Batched feedback can guide a shared update.

**What changes:** Prompts / context, Tools, Workflows. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Prompted task assessments, optionally supplied with reference answers and scores, produce textual feedback for upstream nodes.

**Evaluation.** ArXiv v1 presents GPT-3.5/GPT-4 experiments on HotpotQA, MATH and HumanEval with tools disabled, plus GPT-4-judged creative writing and five software-development tasks scored for executability. Appendix prompts illustrate feedback and configuration edits.

**Boundary.** Textual gradients are analogies, not derivatives or convergence guarantees. Split sizes, optimization budgets and repeated-run uncertainty are insufficiently specified. Same-example rollback does not establish held-out improvement; GPT-3.5 HumanEval trails DSPy. The proof-of-concept does not demonstrate sustained deployment learning.

Reusable prompt optimization and within-instance answer/code/molecule/plan refinement are separate settings; textual gradients are an analogy, not derivatives of model weights.

**Boundary.** The later Nature article is not assumed equivalent to v1. LeetCode prose and Table 1 disagree on baseline accuracy. Compute and voting complicate attribution; simulation scores and retrospective dose metrics establish neither drug safety nor clinical effectiveness. No implementation was executed.

<a id="rest-mcts"></a>

## ReST-MCTS*: LLM Self-Training via Process Reward Guided Tree Search

**2024-06-06 · peer-reviewed · NeurIPS 2024 · adjacent · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.03816)

**Mechanism.** Uses a learned value model to guide tree search with step expansion, rollout and self-criticism. Successful traces fine-tune the policy; inferred values from searched trees train the reward model for the next round. These are persistent parameter updates, distinct from test-time search alone.

**What changes:** Model weights. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Known final answers verify sampled solutions; search reachability and distance produce intermediate value targets. Science initialization also assumes supplied step-by-step solutions are correct and weak-model continuations are wrong.

**Evaluation.** ArXiv v3 reports two training rounds across three backbones on MATH, GPQA Diamond and CEval-Hard, plus GSM8K/MATH500 verifier comparisons and SciBench/SciEval search studies. Token-budget curves and a separate runtime table compare search efficiency.

**Boundary.** Oracle answers and initialization data remain supervision. Reaching a correct final answer does not prove every preceding step valid. Average gains mask task regressions, and matched completion tokens do not imply matched total compute or latency. Some reported values/settings conflict; broad agent tasks and indefinite learning are untested.

**Code / data.** [Official artifact](https://github.com/THUDM/ReST-MCTS) — Official repository README, setup, data-release and training descriptions inspected on 2026-11-09; no research code, datasets or models executed/downloaded. README value-training learning rates differ from the reviewed paper and were not silently reconciled.

**Topics:** model-training, self-play, evaluation. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-11-09.

## Re-ReST: Reflection-Reinforced Self-Training for Language Agents

**2024-06-03 · peer-reviewed · EMNLP 2024 · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.01495)

**Mechanism.** Trains a separate reflector on failed/successful sample pairs, uses one reflection step to repair rejected generations, and fine-tunes the agent on accepted original and repaired trajectories. Improvement persists in model weights; the main inference path uses the agent without reflection.

**What changes:** Model weights. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Reference-answer correctness, environment completion and provided unit tests filter training examples; image-generation feedback comes from a visual evaluation model. Optional GPT-4-initialized comparisons are separate.

**Evaluation.** The final EMNLP paper studies HotpotQA, ALFWorld, MBPP, visual programming and text-to-layout/image generation. Ablations compare more initial samples, trained versus untrained reflection, DPO and a separate test-time self-consistency variant.

**Boundary.** Self-training still needs supplied tasks and training-time feedback. MBPP prompts contain provided unit tests, and visual feedback is not human ground truth. Sampling-efficiency comparisons do not fully account for reflector training. Seed-level uncertainty and broad retention are not established; main training-only reflection and test-time variants should remain distinct.

**Code / data.** [Official artifact](https://github.com/PlusLabNLP/Re-ReST) — Official README inspected on 2026-11-09; it explicitly points to HotpotQA and GQA implementations. Coverage of every paper experiment was not established, and no research code was executed.

**Topics:** model-training, foundations, applications. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-11-09.
