<a id="accumulating-data-model-collapse"></a>

## Is Model Collapse Inevitable? Breaking the Curse of Recursion by Accumulating Real and Synthetic Data

**2024-04-01 · peer-reviewed · COLM 2024 · adjacent · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.01413)

**Mechanism.** Contrasts latest-generation replacement with accumulation of all preceding datasets. In a repeated-design linear regression setting, older data reduce each generation’s added-noise contribution sufficiently to bound expected excess error.

**What changes:** Model weights. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Models train on targets or samples generated by earlier models, retaining the original reference corpus and all successive synthetic batches in the accumulation condition. The data-retention rule is fixed.

**Evaluation.** The detailed arXiv v2 review covers small transformer pretraining on TinyStories, GeoDiff molecular conformations, CelebA VAEs, exact linear-model analysis and dataset-size/temperature/training ablations. Indexed official records establish later COLM 2024 publication; its final body was inaccessible in this pass.

**Boundary.** The bound assumes reused covariates, independent additive noise and underparameterized regression. Growing datasets alter compute and storage; size-matched replacement does not match all generation costs. VAE diversity still degrades, and TinyStories is itself generated text. Bounded error is not unchanged quality or a guarantee for arbitrary self-learning agents.

**Code / data.** ArXiv v2 and its substantive appendices were read in full on 2026-11-09. An official runnable implementation was not established; the author page’s PDF link returned 404 and the final OpenReview body was access-restricted. No training, models or research code were executed.

**Topics:** model-training, safety, evaluation. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-11-09.

**2024-02-27 · peer-reviewed · ACL 2024 · adjacent · benchmark**

[Primary source](https://aclanthology.org/2024.acl-long.747/)

**Mechanism.** Creates persona- and event-grounded simulated conversations, then uses human editing to repair consistency and image alignment. The benchmark tests QA, event summarization and multimodal dialogue generation; a separate training corpus supports the multimodal model experiments.

**What changes:** Memory. **Persistence:** not-applicable. **Learning signal:** Not applicable: analysis or evaluation resource.

It compares truncated/long-context models and RAG, then MiniGPT-5 variants trained on fifty additional unedited conversations. Experiments report a single inference run per model.

## TroVE: Inducing Verifiable and Efficient Toolboxes for Solving Programmatic Tasks

**2024-01-23 · peer-reviewed · ICML 2024 · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.12869)

**Mechanism.** Samples programs in import, create and primitive-only modes, chooses a frequent executable answer with simplicity tie-breaking, and retains its reusable functions. Periodic frequency-based trimming also regenerates earlier solutions affected by removed tools. The model and toolbox-management procedure stay fixed.

**What changes:** Tools, Skills. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Agreement among executed candidate answers, a program-complexity proxy and observed tool reuse; reference answers are used for evaluation rather than per-task tool admission.

**Evaluation.** The final ICML paper covers eleven math, table-QA and visual-reasoning datasets, ordering/selection/rectification ablations, and a six-person verification study. Main results select the best of five runs; some external baselines reuse previously published scores.

**Boundary.** Execution agreement is not correctness verification, and best-run reporting does not estimate typical performance. Retrospective regeneration differs from scoring each streaming prediction once. Supplied primitives and demonstrations matter; complexity is an AST-based proxy. Human verification improves on the tested sample, but broader reliability, lifecycle cost and retention remain unestablished.

## Self-Rewarding Language Models

**2024-01-18 · peer-reviewed · ICML 2024 · adjacent · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.10020)

**Mechanism.** Alternates answer generation, self-judging and DPO updates, changing the shared answering/reward model. The main experiment uses a fixed Llama-2-Chat prompt generator and Claude-2 checkpoint selection, so the loop retains external design and supervision dependencies.

**What changes:** Model weights. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Human-ranked seed data initialize answering and evaluation; the resulting model scores its own candidate answers to create preference pairs.

**Evaluation.** The ICML paper studies a Llama-2-70B seed model and two main DPO rounds using GPT-4 judging, fifty blinded author-rated prompts, MT-Bench, NLP tasks and held-out human preference rankings. A fourth model receives a further AlpacaEval check with smaller gains.

**Boundary.** Responses become longer, potentially influencing preference scores. Gains concentrate outside mathematical reasoning, and several NLP scores regress. Reward-ranking agreement is not correctness or safety assurance; finite iterations, uneven training-data volumes and external checkpoint selection limit claims of autonomous continual improvement.

**Code / data.** Official runnable code was not verified in this source review.

**Topics:** model-training, self-play, evaluation. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-11-09.

## Self-Play Fine-Tuning Converts Weak Language Models to Strong Language Models

**2024-01-02 · peer-reviewed · ICML 2024 · adjacent · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.01335)

**Mechanism.** Optimizes a contrastive log-probability-ratio objective against the previous model, then samples a new opponent dataset from the updated weights. The experiments reuse 50,000 UltraChat prompts with API-generated reference answers; later rounds mix current and preceding generated responses.

**What changes:** Model weights. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Existing reference demonstrations are treated as preferred to responses sampled from the preceding model, without fresh per-pair preference labels.

**Evaluation.** The ICML paper evaluates four rounds on Zephyr-7B using Open LLM Leaderboard tasks, with additional MT-Bench, BBH and OpenBookQA results, data/epoch ablations and optional later DPO. Average gains diminish, and some task scores remain below the SFT baseline.

**Boundary.** Experimental reference answers are synthetic, despite the human-demonstration framing; they remain the fixed target distribution. Idealized theorems assume realizability and global optimization, not guaranteed finite-SGD convergence. DPO comparisons differ in data and supervision; independent training-run uncertainty is not reported.

## When Can LLMs Actually Correct Their Own Mistakes? A Critical Survey of Self-Correction of LLMs

**2024 · peer-reviewed · TACL 2024 · adjacent · survey**

[Primary source](https://aclanthology.org/2024.tacl-1.78/)

**Mechanism.** Organizes inference-time correction around three questions: intrinsic improvement, improvement with external information, and superiority to alternative methods. Its taxonomy checks whether initial answers receive comparable information and strong prompts, and whether correction uses unavailable oracle feedback.

**What changes:** Analysis / no retained update. **Persistence:** not-applicable. **Learning signal:** Not applicable to the survey itself; it distinguishes prompted feedback, external tools/knowledge and trained correction models in the reviewed literature.

**Evaluation.** The TACL article critically compares published protocols and prompt examples, with separate checklists for positive and negative findings. It identifies reliable feedback and trained correction as promising conditions, recognizes decomposable-task exceptions, and recommends direct feedback-quality measurement and compute-matched baselines.

**Boundary.** This is a qualitative review of the 2024 literature, not a new pooled experiment or exhaustive search protocol. Its negative conclusions are conditional on reviewed models, prompts and task properties. The best-initial-answer criterion requires judgment; inference-time correction does not itself demonstrate persistent learning or impossibility for later models.

## MemGPT: Towards LLMs as Operating Systems

**2023-10-12 · preprint · adjacent · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.08560)

**Mechanism.** Separates active context from archival and recall storage. Function calls page information in and out, edit working memory, and request successive inference steps; persistent records support later conversations without changing model weights.

**What changes:** Memory. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Conversation history, retrieved documents, memory-pressure notices and function outcomes guide a frozen model in choosing memory edits and searches.

**Evaluation.** Augmented Multi-Session Chat tests recall and persona-based opening messages; document QA uses 50 NaturalQuestions questions, and synthetic nested-key retrieval varies nesting with 30 orderings. GPT-4-based memory retrieval improves over summary-only chat baselines; function-calling ability affects results.

**Boundary.** Chat baselines see lossy summaries while MemGPT can search full history, with different answer instructions. The recall judge is permissive; engagement is measured by similarity, not demonstrated user satisfaction. Limited benchmark horizons and premature search stopping do not establish reliable unlimited memory or reusable procedural learning.

**Code / data.** Code availability not verified in this review.

**Topics:** foundations, memory, architecture. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-11-09.

**2023-10-05 · peer-reviewed · ICLR 2024 · adjacent · paper**

**Mechanism.** Compiles declarative LM modules by bootstrapping and selecting demonstrations. Composed optimizers can ensemble programs or fine-tune smaller models. Optimized prompts, program configurations or weights persist, while the developer supplies the task decomposition and metric.

**What changes:** Prompts / context, Workflows, Model weights. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Developer-defined metrics and training examples filter generated execution traces; optional teacher programs supply intermediate demonstrations or fine-tuning targets.

**Evaluation.** GSM8K and HotpotQA comparisons cover prompting, bootstrapping, ensembles and T5 distillation. Ensembles and search add computation, and strong teachers or answer labels remain inputs. This review concerns the original v1 paper, not every feature of current DSPy.

## Self-Taught Optimizer (STOP): Recursively Self-Improving Code Generation

**2023-10-03 · peer-reviewed · COLM 2024 · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.02304)

**Mechanism.** Applies an LLM-assisted program improver to its own source, retaining the resulting improver for subsequent rounds and tasks. The scaffold changes; the language-model weights and evaluation objective remain fixed.

**What changes:** Agent code. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** A fixed meta-utility scores how well an improver revises downstream programs under externally set budgets.

**Evaluation.** ArXiv v3 reports five independent GPT-4 runs on ten-bit noisy parity, held-out instances, selected-improver transfer to five tasks and weaker-model comparisons. A separate 10,000-proposal safety study counts syntactic indicators without executing those proposals.

**Boundary.** Weaker models often deteriorate and transfer uses one selected improver. Reported gains are utility-specific; the released quadratic-assignment evaluator rewards a larger objective while its seed minimizes it. Sandbox-flag counts are not demonstrated escapes, and recursive progress is not guaranteed.

**2023-10-03 · peer-reviewed · ICLR 2024 · adjacent · paper**

[Primary source](https://proceedings.iclr.cc/paper_files/paper/2024/hash/8b4add8b0aa8749d80a34ca5d941c355-Abstract-Conference.html)

**Mechanism.** Evaluates within-task revision without external correctness feedback, contrasting it with oracle-controlled stopping, multi-agent debate and stronger initial prompts. No persistent memory or weight update is learned by the evaluated correction loop.

**What changes:** Analysis / no retained update. **Persistence:** within-task. **Learning signal:** Not applicable: analysis or evaluation resource.

**Evaluation.** ArXiv v2 tests 2023 GPT-3.5/GPT-4 variants and Llama-2 on GSM8K, CommonSenseQA and closed-book HotpotQA. It measures correct-to-incorrect revisions, compares debate with response-count-matched voting, and examines concept coverage on CommonGen-Hard.

**Boundary.** Most non-GPT-3.5 tests use 200 examples, or 100 HotpotQA questions. Matching response counts does not match token cost. The CommonGen comparison also changes sentence versus paragraph instructions. These bounded negative results do not establish impossibility for later models, trained correctors or external feedback.

## Promptbreeder: Self-Referential Self-Improvement via Prompt Evolution

**2023-09-28 · peer-reviewed · ICML 2024 · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.16797)

**Mechanism.** A tournament population evolves task instructions and the mutation instructions that generate successors, including hypermutation and reconstruction from worked solutions. Weights, evaluation rules and prompt topology remain fixed; reusable prompts and demonstrations carry the changes.

**What changes:** Prompts / context. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Accuracy on sampled training examples selects task prompts, mutation prompts and optional successful demonstrations.

**Evaluation.** The ICML paper evaluates arithmetic, commonsense reasoning, ETHOS and 24 instruction-induction tasks, with initialization/operator ablations and GPT-3.5 follow-ups. Main ablations measure average population fitness during search; GPT-3.5 follow-ups test the best training-scoring prompt.

**Boundary.** Ablation fitness is not independent evidence of held-out improvement from each operator. Initialization contributes strongly, some baselines use historical models, and search has substantial token cost. Changing mutation prompts does not demonstrate unbounded improvement of the evaluator or outer algorithm.

**2023-08-20 · peer-reviewed · AAAI 2024 · core · paper**

During the main held-out evaluation, the full insight list and similar successful trajectories condition a frozen actor. Additional test-time retries are evaluated separately.

## Reinforced Self-Training (ReST) for Language Modeling

**2023-08-17 · preprint · adjacent · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.08998)

**Mechanism.** Alternates costly generation rounds with multiple offline updates on increasingly filtered data. The strongest reward-score variant uses ordinary supervised negative log-likelihood on selected outputs. Model weights change; retraining the reward model with fresh human feedback is proposed future work.

**What changes:** Model weights. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** A fixed, human-preference-trained Metric X model scores generated translations; original reference translations remain in the training mixture.

**Evaluation.** ArXiv v2 studies three translation language pairs across IWSLT, WMT and an author-internal benchmark, comparing losses, thresholds, growth rounds, PPO and best-of-N decoding. Human ratings improve over the supervised baseline but rank variants differently from the learned reward.

**Boundary.** Additional growth can increase reward while reducing human-rated gains, and sentence repetition can exploit the reward model. Large synthetic corpora and repeated fine-tuning remain costly. The study does not establish a generally superior RL algorithm or a reward signal that improves itself.

<a id="robocat"></a>

## RoboCat: A Self-Improving Generalist Agent for Robotic Manipulation

**2023-06-20 · peer-reviewed · TMLR 2024 · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.11706)

**Mechanism.** Fine-tunes a visual goal-conditioned generalist into specialists, collects experience with their frozen policies, then retrains on old and new data. The policy also predicts future image tokens. Humans control collection and offline training; no parameter learning occurs during physical interaction.

**What changes:** Model weights. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Behavior cloning uses human demonstrations, expert-agent and self-generated trajectories, plus visual hindsight goals. Human-labeled success classifiers support collection and goal selection; reported real-world evaluation is manually scored.

**Evaluation.** The reviewed paper tests simulation and real-robot manipulation, held-out task and embodiment adaptation, and one self-improvement iteration. A smaller controlled study compares demonstrations alone with added self-generated data; full-model analyses cover transfer, perception, resets and task difficulty.

**Boundary.** The 100–1000 demonstrations per new task sit on top of extensive prior data and checkpoint evaluation. Some insertion/building tasks remain weak. The model card reports no independent training repeats; baseline data and capacity differ, and some reported aggregates/labels conflict. Controlled laboratory results do not establish open-world or lifelong autonomous adaptation.

**Code / data.** Official runnable code was not established in this review; no installation, training, or research execution was performed.

**Topics:** foundations, model-training, skills, continual-learning, applications. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-11-09.

<a id="model-collapse"></a>

## AI models collapse when trained on recursively generated data

**2023-05-27 · peer-reviewed · Nature 2024 · adjacent · paper**

[Primary source](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-024-07566-y)

**Mechanism.** Analyzes how finite resampling, restricted model families and fitting error can alter distributions across generations. Under stated fixed-sample Gaussian assumptions, expected distributional error diverges and fitted covariance collapses; these are distinct theoretical statements.

**What changes:** Model weights. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Repeated fitting uses generated samples from earlier models; experiments vary original-data retention, while the central discrete and Gaussian theory uses latest-generation replacement.

**Evaluation.** The corrected Nature article, full supplement and 2025 correction were inspected. Experiments include five seeded OPT-125M fine-tuning chains, Gaussian mixtures and MNIST VAEs, with retention and repetition controls. Supplementary Gaussian experiments also compare fixed sampling from an accumulating pool with fitting the whole pool.

**Boundary.** The 2025 correction specifies beta=gamma=0 for the main theoretical replacement setting. Language experiments use beam-generated continuations of original prefixes; retention comparisons also change training epochs. Finite results include plateaus and partial recovery. These findings do not prove failure of every filtered, verified or data-accumulating learning loop.

**Code / data.** [Official artifact](https://zenodo.org/records/10866595) — Author-linked Zenodo code archive v0.1, its file inventory and README at b48c90a inspected on 2026-11-09. The README says hardware/Slurm-specific parts were removed. The archive predates the final Nature article and correction; no code, notebook, dataset or model was executed.

**Topics:** model-training, safety, evaluation. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-11-09.

<a id="llms-as-tool-makers"></a>

## Large Language Models as Tool Makers

**2023-05-26 · peer-reviewed · ICLR 2024 · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.17126)

**Mechanism.** A stronger model proposes Python tools, verifies them on examples and packages calling demonstrations for a cheaper user model. Tools persist in a functional cache. Verification retries repair test calls rather than the function; new task classes may need labels from a strong model or human.

**What changes:** Tools. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Labeled task demonstrations and validation answers guide program generation and function-call tests; a dispatcher identifies known or unseen task types.

**Evaluation.** ArXiv v2 uses six task families with three training, three validation and 240 test examples each. It reports tool-making success over five trials, downstream accuracy and separate dispatcher tests on mixed 100-instance samples.

**Boundary.** Dispatcher classification is not an end-to-end continual-learning trial. Three validation examples cannot certify general tool correctness, and logical-deduction accuracy remains below GPT-4 CoT. Cost arguments amortize creation using historical API rates; the scheduling task is a two-person time-slot template, not real email interaction.

**Code / data.** [Official artifact](https://github.com/ctlllll/LLM-ToolMaker) — Official repository linked and its public page inspected; not executed.

**Topics:** foundations, tools, skills. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-11-09.

<a id="voyager"></a>

## Voyager: An Open-Ended Embodied Agent with Large Language Models

**2023-05-25 · peer-reviewed · TMLR 2024 · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.16291)

**Mechanism.** Stores successful Minecraft programs in a persistent skill library indexed by generated descriptions. Retrieved skills support composition and up to four code attempts per objective. Models and controller logic remain fixed; the setup supplies high-level control APIs and a hand-specified curriculum warmup.

**What changes:** Skills, Tools. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Environment state, execution errors and a GPT-4 task critic guide program revision. A fixed curriculum prompt proposes new objectives from accumulated progress and current state.

**Evaluation.** Three exploration runs measure item acquisition, tech-tree progress and traversal. Separate tests reset inventory and world while retaining the library for four new goals, and also transfer it to an AutoGPT baseline. Ablations examine curriculum, skills and feedback.

**Boundary.** Text state, control primitives and inventory-preserving recovery distinguish this from pixel-based embodied learning. Prompt counts are not total compute. Diamond-tool exploration succeeds in one of three runs; finite transfer tests do not establish lifelong retention. State-based criticism can misjudge success, and 3D construction examples use human guidance.

**Code / data.** [Official artifact](https://github.com/MineDojo/Voyager) — Official README inspected on 2026-11-09; it documents Minecraft/Fabric, Python/Node dependencies, checkpointing and separate learned-library inference. No game, research code or model API was run; arXiv v2 is the inspected body.

**Topics:** foundations, skills, tools, continual-learning. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-11-09.

<a id="creator"></a>

## CREATOR: Tool Creation for Disentangling Abstract and Concrete Reasoning of Large Language Models

**2023-05-23 · peer-reviewed · Findings of EMNLP 2023 · adjacent · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.14318)

**Mechanism.** Separates reusable Python tool construction from problem-specific calls, executes their combination and revises it after runtime errors. Weights stay fixed. A separate transfer experiment supplies a correct tool from a related problem to other members of a constructed problem group.

**What changes:** Tools. **Persistence:** both. **Learning signal:** Problem descriptions, hand-corrected demonstrations and runtime error tracebacks guide tool creation and repair.

**Evaluation.** The ACL v2 paper tests numerical-answer subsets of MATH and TabMWP, a 2,000-item synthetic Creation Challenge, and 300 grouped transfer questions. It separates execution success from answer accuracy and compares hints, rectification and entangled-stage baselines.

**Boundary.** The numerical subsets cover approximately 80% of the original benchmarks. Transfer uses a tool selected as correct; it does not test unguided library retrieval. Hint availability and CoT change outcomes, and the separated design is not uniformly better. Runtime success alone does not establish semantic correctness.

**Code / data.** [Official artifact](https://github.com/qiancheng0/CREATOR) — Official repository linked and its public page inspected; not executed.

**Topics:** foundations, tools. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-11-09.

<a id="memorybank"></a>

## MemoryBank: Enhancing Large Language Models with Long-Term Memory

**2023-05-17 · peer-reviewed · AAAI 2024 · adjacent · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.10250)

**Mechanism.** Stores dialogue records, daily/global summaries and user profiles, retrieves them with dense embeddings, and proposes exponential time decay with stronger retention after recall. SiliconFriend separately LoRA-tunes open models on 38,000 psychological dialogues before integrating memory.

**What changes:** Memory. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Past conversations, generated event/personality summaries, elapsed time and recall frequency shape stored context and proposed memory retention.

**Evaluation.** ArXiv v3 reports 194 manually written questions over ten simulated days for fifteen synthetic users, split equally between English and Chinese. Human ratings compare three SiliconFriend backbones on retrieval, correctness and coherence; real-user examples illustrate recall and personalization.

**Boundary.** The quantitative study does not isolate the forgetting rule or compare memory versus no-memory under a matched backbone. Synthetic probes and selected empathy examples are not clinical validation or general skill learning. The reviewed body is arXiv v3; current AAAI body access was restricted, so publication-version equivalence is not assumed.

**Code / data.** Code availability not verified in this review.

**Topics:** foundations, memory. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-11-09.

<a id="generative-agents"></a>

## Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior

**2023-04-07 · peer-reviewed · UIST 2023 · adjacent · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.03442)

**Mechanism.** Stores observations, plans and recursive reflections in a persistent memory stream. Recency, importance and embedding relevance determine retrieval; a frozen language model generates plans, dialogue and reactions from that context.

**What changes:** Memory. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Observed sandbox events, model-scored memory importance and model-generated reflections influence later retrieval and plans; identities and initial goals are human-authored.

**Evaluation.** Twenty-five agents interact for two simulated days. One hundred evaluators rank interview responses from the full architecture, ablations and crowdworker-written baselines. Ablations reuse histories generated by the full system; separate descriptive analyses examine information diffusion, relationships and party attendance.

**Boundary.** Believability is not factual accuracy or increasing task competence. Ablations do not independently rerun the social simulation, and the human baseline is not expert performance. Retrieval failures, embellished memories, over-cooperation, simulation cost and short observation horizons limit claims of reliable lifelong learning.

**Code / data.** [Official artifact](https://github.com/joonspk-research/generative_agents) — Official repository inspected on 2026-10-28; not executed. UIST 2023 publication is verified from the official proceedings; the earlier ACM access limitation is retained in the review history.

**Topics:** foundations, memory, architecture. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-11-09.

<a id="self-refine"></a>

## Self-Refine: Iterative Refinement with Self-Feedback

**2023-03-30 · peer-reviewed · NeurIPS 2023 · adjacent · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.17651)

**Mechanism.** Alternates drafting, feedback and revision while retaining the current task history. No weights or cross-task memory are updated; stopping and output selection vary across the evaluated tasks.

**What changes:** Analysis / no retained update. **Persistence:** within-task. **Learning signal:** The same model generates task-specific critiques using curated few-shot examples; separate oracle experiments additionally use answer correctness to control refinement.

**Evaluation.** Seven text/code tasks with automatic measures, model preferences and blinded author assessments; feedback ablations, repeated-sampling controls and weaker-model analysis. Main-table math gains are only 0–0.2 percentage points. Oracle-guided math results in Appendices H/O are a different setting.

**Boundary.** The headline average combines heterogeneous metrics and is not a universal accuracy gain. Prompt examples include human-written feedback and revisions. Quality can regress and weaker models fail to refine. Appendix J labels its intervals 95% in the caption and 99% in the text, leaving their confidence level ambiguous.

**Code / data.** No implementation link independently inspected for this entry; this does not establish that none exists.

**Topics:** foundations, evaluation, prompts. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-11-09.

<a id="reflexion"></a>

## Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning

**2023-03-20 · peer-reviewed · NeurIPS 2023 · adjacent · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.11366)

**Mechanism.** A fixed actor retries the same task using verbal reflections produced from earlier attempts and evaluation feedback. The episodic buffer retains only recent reflections, usually three for interactive/reasoning tasks and one for coding; model weights stay fixed.

**What changes:** Memory. **Persistence:** within-task. **Learning signal:** Task-dependent feedback: environment completion and heuristics for ALFWorld, reference-answer exact-match judgments for HotpotQA, and self-generated executable tests for programming.

**Evaluation.** Reports cumulative ALFWorld and HotpotQA improvement, coding results after internal testing/revision, and feedback/memory ablations. The coding pass@1 result means one final submitted program after internal attempts, not one generation or a matched-compute comparison.

**Boundary.** The experiments do not establish cross-task learning. Gains depend on feedback quality: MBPP Python degrades, WebShop shows little improvement, and the tested smaller coding model does not improve. Incorrect tests can cause premature acceptance or harmful edits. Selected successful reflections are not causal proof of faithful error diagnosis.

**Code / data.** [Official artifact](https://github.com/noahshinn/reflexion) — Official README inspected on 2026-11-09; it documents separate reasoning, decision-making and programming experiments and historical logs. No research code, API calls or benchmark experiments were executed.

**Topics:** foundations, memory. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-11-09.

<a id="toolformer"></a>

## Toolformer: Language Models Can Teach Themselves to Use Tools

**2023-02-09 · peer-reviewed · NeurIPS 2023 · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.04761)

**Mechanism.** Samples API calls into ordinary text, executes and filters them using future-token loss reduction, and fine-tunes GPT-J on the augmented corpus. Learned tool invocation persists in weights; the tool set and data-selection heuristics remain fixed.

**What changes:** Model weights. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Human-seeded API examples propose calls; tool responses are retained when they reduce loss on subsequent corpus tokens, then become fine-tuning data.

**Evaluation.** LAMA, arithmetic, QA, multilingual and temporal tasks, plus language-model perplexity and size/decoding analyses. Gains vary by task: QA remains below GPT-3, and some multilingual results regress relative to GPT-J. Evaluation allows at most one call and encourages it when the API token is among the top ten.

**Boundary.** Training calls are sampled independently, so chained or interactive tool use is not learned. Benchmarks selectively disable tools and use relaxed answer matching. Tool costs are not optimized; API outputs can be noisy, and externally supplied QA/translation models contribute capability. Zero-shot downstream evaluation is not zero-demonstration training.

**Code / data.** Official runnable code was not verified in this source review.

**Topics:** foundations, tools, model-training. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-11-09.

<a id="self-instruct"></a>

## Self-Instruct: Aligning Language Models with Self-Generated Instructions

**2022-12-20 · peer-reviewed · ACL 2023 · adjacent · paper**

[Primary source](https://aclanthology.org/2023.acl-long.754/)

**Mechanism.** Expands a task pool with GPT-3 generations, identifies classification tasks, generates inputs/outputs in different orders and filters overlap or malformed examples. A subsequent offline fine-tuning stage updates the original model; the data-generation model is not continually retrained during pool construction.

**What changes:** Model weights. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** 175 author-written seed tasks guide a fixed model to generate instructions and examples; heuristic filtering selects data for later supervised fine-tuning.

**Evaluation.** The ACL paper reports 52,445 instructions and 82,439 instances, 119 Super-NaturalInstructions test tasks and 252 author-written user tasks. The headline 33.1-point gain is ROUGE-L, while the user-task comparison uses blinded author ratings.

**Boundary.** Only 54% of 200 sampled generated examples had all fields rated valid by one author. Human-evaluation figures report one of two raters; the near-InstructGPT result concerns the older 001 model. Filtering is not correctness verification, and the closed fine-tuning API limits reproducibility.

**Code / data.** [Official artifact](https://github.com/yizhongw/self-instruct) — Official repository page checked; code and training were not executed.

**Topics:** foundations, model-training. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-11-09.

<a id="constitutional-ai"></a>

## Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback

**2022-12-15 · preprint · adjacent · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.08073)

**Mechanism.** Fine-tunes on constitution-guided response revisions, then fits a preference model to mixed human-helpfulness and AI-harmlessness labels and trains a policy with RL. Learned weights persist; the constitution, training procedure and evaluation rules are externally chosen.

**What changes:** Model weights. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Human-written principles and few-shot examples guide AI critiques and harmlessness comparisons; human helpfulness preference labels and human/model-generated prompts remain training inputs.

**Evaluation.** Crowdworker comparisons assess helpfulness and harmlessness across model sizes and training snapshots, alongside critique/revision controls, AI-label evaluations and a learned harmfulness scorer. Evaluators explicitly prefer non-evasive answers when similarly harmless, unlike the earlier baseline-labeling instructions.

**Boundary.** This removes human harmlessness preference labels, not all human supervision. Over-training can produce boilerplate and overly harsh replies; critiques can be inaccurate. Different initialization and feedback-model choices complicate isolated component attribution, and finite red-team evaluations do not guarantee safety under later self-modification.

**Code / data.** Official runnable code was not verified in this source review.

**Topics:** foundations, model-training, safety. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-11-09.

<a id="react"></a>

## ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models

**2022-10-06 · peer-reviewed · ICLR 2023 · adjacent · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.03629)

**Mechanism.** Interleaves language reasoning, tool actions and observations to revise a plan within a task. The main prompted variant keeps weights fixed; the separately evaluated fine-tuned variant retains learned weights across tasks.

**What changes:** Model weights. **Persistence:** both. **Learning signal:** Environment observations guide the prompted task loop; a separate offline experiment uses 3,000 answer-correct generated trajectories to fine-tune smaller models.

**Evaluation.** HotpotQA, FEVER, 134 ALFWorld games and 500 WebShop instructions, with reasoning-only/action-only controls and fine-tuning comparisons. ReAct alone trails CoT on HotpotQA; hybrids perform better. The headline ALFWorld result is the best of six prompt configurations, distinct from their mean.

**Boundary.** Prompted interaction does not itself retain learning between tasks. Human-authored demonstrations and external retrieval support performance; retrieval failures and reasoning loops remain. Offline fine-tuning is distinct from self-directed online improvement, and interpretable traces do not guarantee faithful reasoning.

**Code / data.** No implementation link independently inspected for this entry; this does not establish that none exists.

**Topics:** foundations, tools. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-11-09.

<a id="star"></a>

## STaR: Bootstrapping Reasoning With Reasoning

**2022-03-28 · peer-reviewed · NeurIPS 2022 · adjacent · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.14465)

**Mechanism.** Generates reasoning traces, keeps traces ending in the reference answer, and fine-tunes on them. Failed problems can be retried with the answer supplied as a hint; each outer iteration retrains from the original base model on the newly collected traces.

**What changes:** Model weights. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Known correct answers filter generated rationales; answer hints support rationalization of failed examples.

**Evaluation.** GPT-J experiments cover arithmetic, CommonsenseQA development accuracy and GSM8K test accuracy. Ablations examine answer hints, prompting and sampling; a small human study ranks explanations only for questions both compared models answered correctly.

**Boundary.** Answer filtering does not certify rationale validity or faithfulness; the appendices document circular and incorrect reasoning with correct answers. Results depend on pretrained ability, supplied labels, prompt seeds and training schedules. Rationalization adds little on GSM8K, and the study does not establish stable continual improvement.

**Code / data.** [Official artifact](https://github.com/ezelikman/STaR) — Official README inspected on 2026-11-09; it identifies the STaR training wrapper and largely inherited mesh-transformer-jax setup. No model, training code or benchmark execution was performed.

**Topics:** foundations, model-training. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-11-09.

<a id="alphago-zero"></a>

## Mastering the game of Go without human knowledge

**2017-10-19 · peer-reviewed · Nature 2017 · adjacent · paper**

[Primary source](https://www.nature.com/articles/nature24270)

**Mechanism.** Alternates search-guided self-play with gradient updates to a shared policy/value network. Recent games are replayed to fit improved move distributions and outcomes. The training/search algorithm and network design remain externally specified.

**What changes:** Model weights. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** MCTS visit distributions and scored self-play outcomes train a policy/value network; a 400-game comparison gate admits new data-generating checkpoints above 55% wins.

**Evaluation.** The 3-day, 20-block run generated 4.9 million games and defeated AlphaGo Lee 100–0; a separate 40-day, 40-block run generated 29 million games and defeated AlphaGo Master 89–11. Architecture controls use fixed self-play data, and move prediction differs from playing strength.

**Boundary.** No human game demonstrations are used for the principal training runs, but exact rules, legal moves, board symmetries, architecture and search-parameter tuning remain inputs. Four TPUs describe the playing configuration, not total training compute; optimization used 64 GPU workers and 19 CPU parameter servers. Evidence is specific to Go.

**Code / data.** Official runnable code was not verified in this source review.

**Topics:** foundations, self-play, model-training. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-11-09.
